Melania Trump’s top aide has revealed their true thoughts about Natalie Harp, whose close relationship with her boss, Donald Trump, has fueled recent speculation.

Harp, Trump’s executive assistant, has been thrust into the political spotlight in recent weeks with reports that she slept in the locker room at Trump’s Bedminster golf club and even hopped in the trunk of an SUV to stay close to the president.

Senator Jon Ossoff, a Democrat from Georgia up for re-election, made headlines for his quip about Trump, telling a crowd in Atlanta last month, “He doesn’t want to do the job. He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie.”

Marc Beckman, senior advisor to Melania, dismissed any rumors that her husband’s relationship with Harp is anything but above board on an episode of conservative media personality Stella Escobedo’s YouTube show released Tuesday.

“The mainstream media…they’re endlessly obsessed with garbage tabloid gossip about Natalie Harp, who, by the way, is a hard-working, loyal White House aide to President Trump—a cancer survivor—who POTUS helped get off labeled treatment for and saved her life. I mean, what do you make of that?” Escobedo asked Beckman.

open image in gallery Melania Trump’s top aide has revealed their true thoughts about Natalie Harp, whose close relationship with her boss, Donald Trump, has fueled speculation ( Getty Images )

Harp, who says she was diagnosed with bone cancer, gained national attention in 2019 for crediting Trump for saving her life with a law he signed in 2018 that provided her access to experimental treatments.

“The liberal media is ridiculous. They don’t know anything about the first lady’s personal and private life,” Beckman told Escobedo. “They don’t even take the time to put us on air to cover these incredible achievements that our first lady has accomplished.”

“What they need to do is look in the mirror because they’re all attacking this hardworking, very talented, very intelligent person in Natalie Harp,” he said, adding that the mainstream media is “obsessed with the gossip with the first family. And I can tell you firsthand that it’s time for them to become journalists and stop looking at the gossip.”

open image in gallery Melania's aide accused the mainstream media of 'attacking this hardworking, very talented, very intelligent person in Natalie Harp' ( Getty Images )

The public started to pay closer attention to Harp after The Washington Post reported last month that she was one of the select few who got to ride with Trump in a catering truck that transported them from Air Force One to a smaller jet amid a potential assassination threat from Iran while they were leaving the NATO summit in Turkey. During Trump’s escape, Air Force One, which carried unsuspecting D.C. reporters and senior Trump officials, served as a decoy.

Harp —who reportedly received a $45,000 holiday cash gift from Trump — wrote in a letter to Trump in 2023, “You are all that matters to me,” The New York Times reported shortly after the president’s 2024 election victory in an article announcing that she would follow him to the White House after joining his team in 2022.

While Harp seems to never leave Trump’s side, Melania has been largely absent from the public eye during her husband’s second term.

Over the summer, Melania missed Senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral, the rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner, and the dignified transfer of the remains of four service members killed in the Middle East.

NBC News reported on August 17 that Melania has made about half as many public appearances as she did at that point in Trump’s first term.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
News.content:
Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

News.title: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal
News.content:
In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

News.title: Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner
News.content:
Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

News.title: Gay does enough to earn another chance as England dominate again
News.content:
There are two places up for grabs in England’s top three and three players vying: Gay, Jordan Cox and Jacob Bethell, who spent the day on the players’ balcony dropping a reminder of his looming return. A hundred for Durham by Ben McKinney, the one challenger outside of the squad, tweaked the ante up further.

One of Cox or Gay will make way for Bethell when England begin their next series in Johannesburg on December 17, which will be the first Test of the Stephen Fleming era and the first big call he has to make. Cox was on the up after scores of 75 at Headingley and 55 in the first innings at Lord’s, looking the part at No 3. Gay’s luck had run out with a grubber in the second Test and he wasted a couple of 30s in other innings. Cox has opened in first-class cricket and Bethell could also take on the role of Ben Duckett’s partner. The squeeze was on.

But Cox perhaps got a little ahead of himself and played what could be a costly, impetuous shot at Mohammad Abbas to fall for six and hand Gay a chance. Neither Cox nor Gay have been tested on the back foot by genuine pace which will happen at the Wanderers in December but their performances have to be judged against the backdrop of a seam bowlers’ summer. Gay is averaging 27.1 from 10 innings, a number probably worth another 10 runs given the conditions.

His dismissal 20 minutes before the close, playing on driving away from his body, was the one time his footwork was non-existent and Razaullah deserved the breakthrough for coming back and hitting 90mph after tea following so little first-class cricket and a rushed call-up amidst the bloodletting.

News.title: I got a first look at Apple’s new £2k iPhone – it’s not just the price that makes it stand out
News.content:
Apple has entered the foldable phone race with the iPhone Duo, following years of speculation about whether the company would ever bend its famously rigid design philosophy.

Barely a month after Samsung dropped its latest Galaxy Z Fold 8, this is the moment Apple stakes its claim in a category it has notoriously avoided for the last decade. I was at the launch event at Apple’s HQ in Cupertino, California for a first look.

Similar in size to a British passport, the new smartphone unfolds like a miniature book to reveal a large 7.6-inch inner screen. When closed, it’s shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, and when opened, it resembles a small iPad.

What makes the iPhone Duo worth your attention isn’t just that it’s the first hinged phone with an Apple logo, but that it addresses some of the biggest frustrations currently plaguing folding mobiles.

You can barely see the crease on the inner display, and it doesn’t look like a cheap plastic sheet. It’s intuitive to use, and fully waterproof, which is rare among rivals. Whether all that justifies a £2,000 price tag, however, is another question entirely.

News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

Sports.title: Moment mass brawl erupts at Sunday League football match with players throwing punches as game descends into violence
Sports.content:
THIS is the moment a huge football brawl broke out as players and others traded savage blows after a Sunday league match erupted into chaos.

The brawl spilled into A&E when a man allegedly stormed into hospital and attacked medics treating casualties from the scrap.



Footage shows spectators ducking under a makeshift rope barrier separating the players from the pitch before piling into the fray.

Within seconds, large groups of men and women are seen charging onto the pitch as the row erupts into a chaotic mass scrap.



The wounded were then rushed into the nearby emergency department, triggering a frantic scramble as every available member of staff battled to cope with the sudden surge.

But the mayhem allegedly followed them through the hospital doors.



One man is accused of barging into the emergency unit, hurling abuse and assaulting healthcare workers before cops were called to bring the situation under control.

The original violence erupted on a sports pitch beside the community hospital in Bulnes, Chile, on Sunday, September 6.

The Ñuble Health Service and bosses at Bulnes Community Family Health Hospital have since condemned the shocking scenes.

In a joint statement, they voiced their “absolute rejection of any form of violence against health workers” following the alleged attack inside the emergency department.



Officials said treatment continued despite the turmoil “thanks to the commitment and professionalism of the teams”.

Authorities are now preparing to file a criminal complaint against the person accused of attacking hospital staff.

The clubs involved have not been named and officials have not revealed how many people were hurt in the football brawl.



It remains unclear whether anyone involved in the initial clash was arrested.

Anyone with footage or information about the explosive incident has been urged to contact police.

It comes after a Colombia football game was suspended for almost an hour after fans invaded the pitch to brawl with sticks and chairs.

The top flight clash between Santa Fe and America de Cali on Saturday had to be halted after chaotic scenes involving supporters.

Violence initially broke out in the stands midway through the first half as fans from both sides scrapped over claims that one group had their flag stolen.



Fighting then spilled out onto the pitch at the El Campin stadium in Bogota and a mass brawl erupted.

Fans charged onto the grass holding sticks, chairs and other objects as they were seen launching them at their rival supporters.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis sacks his 25TH manager in 16 years just seven games into club’s season
Sports.content:
EVANGELOS MARINAKIS has sacked his 25TH manager in just 16 years just seven games into the season.

The Nottingham Forest owner is also the boss of Greek giants Olympiacos and Portuguese side Rio Ave.



The club have announced that manager Jose Luis Mendilibar has left his role in the dugout.

Mendilibar, 65, had led the club to a Conference League triumph in 2024 before winning a domestic treble the following season.



But after failing to qualify for the Champions League this season a change in manager has been made.

Olympiacos confirmed the decision with a statement which honoured his achievements.



It then went on to state that his time at the club was over.

A segment said: “But in football, as in life, there are cycles that eventually close. But what resonates in eternity is what you have achieved.

“The appreciation, respect and love of the OLYMPIC family will accompany you forever, General, along with the strong emotions that united us and are eternal.

“Thank you for everything.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The Spanish manager becomes the 25TH manager to be axed by Marinakis in the last 16 years.

Last season, the Greek businessman went through four managers at Nottingham Forest.

Nuno Espirito Santo was sacked early in the season before his replacement Ange Postecoglou was axed after just eight winless games.

Former Burnley and Everton boss Sean Dyche was then hired before getting in the firing line after 25 games.



The East Midlands side survived relegation with Vítor Pereira in charge but the club parted with him after the season ended.

Oliver Glasner has since taken charge at the City Ground following his exit from Crystal Palace.



Olympiacos have dropped into the Europa League and will start their campaign against Polish side Jagiellonia Białystok.

The club is currently third in the Greek Super League after three games in which they have won two and drawn one.

Sports.title: Chelsea ratings: Palmer shows Blues what they’re missing when he doesn’t start but Gusto can’t stop giving the ball away
Sports.content:
CHELSEA staged an admirable comeback as they beat Leeds 6-3 in a goalfest, with the second half substitutes making the difference.

Half-time sub Cole Palmer starred as he notched two in as many minutes to draw the Blues level early in the second half.



The visitors found themselves 1-0 up after 23 minutes as new signing Tarik Muharemovic headed in from a corner.

And after his team were totally dominated in the first half, Xabi Alonso brought on regular starters Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Reece James and Pedro Neto.



Despite Leeds doubling their lead three minutes into the second period, they had completely lost it just 12 minutes later, as a Cole Palmer double and convincing finish from Neto put the Blues in control.

Five minutes later Danny Welbeck finished smartly, giving Chelsea one foot in the next round. And despite Leeds’ attempted fightback via Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Valentin Barco smashed in from Rogers’ cross to make sure of the result.

Welbeck then grabbed his second of the game in the dying stages to give Chelsea 6.

Sports.title: Fans realise what Marcos Llorente named his dog as he torments Liverpool again – and Steven Gerrard makes cheeky quip
Sports.content:
FANS have discovered that Atletico Madrid star Marcos Llorente has named his dog Anfield.

The pet’s cheeky name is another dig as the 31-year-old continues to torment Liverpool.



Llorente opted to name his pug after the iconic Premier League stadium after knocking Liverpool out of the Champions League in 2020.

He bagged a brace as Atletico secured a 3-2 win in extra-ime to march into the quarter-finals of the European competition.



While the Spanish side ultimately fell 2-1 against RB Leipzig in the following round, Anfield has remained a happy hunting ground for Llorente.

Llorente bagged another brace against Liverpool during last season’s Champions League group stage.

This was followed by a fifth Anfield goal in the 17th minute of Atletico’s opening-round visit to Merseyside during this season’s campaign.

The defender’s pug’s name has led several fans on social media to note Llorente’s “special connection” with Anfield.

One fan on X said: “Marcos Llorente owns Anfield like it’s his local five-a-side cage, absolute menace.”

Another commented: “Named his dog Anfield and keeps feeding it goals.”

Llorente’s continued form at the historic ground prompted TNT Sports commentator Darren Fletcher to mention the pooch’s name.

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard was then quick to suggest what he would name a pet if he followed in the same vein.

Gerrard said: “I’d call mine Goodison!”

However, only three of Gerrard’s ten goals scored in the Merseyside Derby actually came at Goodison Park, with the other seven being scored at Anfield.

Unfortunately for Llorente, his goal was not enough as Liverpool recovered to claim a 2-1 win against the LaLiga side.



To make matters worse, the sides will be banned from facing each other at Anfield in next season’s league phase after a Uefa rule change.

Liverpool are next set to host Fulham in the Premier League on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Atletico will travel away to Real Sociedad for a LaLiga clash on Sunday.

Sports.title: Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola after £123m Liverpool signing suffers worrying-looking injury in first start
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL have cause for concern as new £123million signing Bradley Barcola was subbed off with an injury in their win over Atletico Madrid.

The Reds came back to beat the Spanish giants 2-1 thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister cancelling out Marcos Llorente‘s opener.



But Barcola was withdrawn just before the hour mark after clutching his left calf.

The Frenchman was replaced by fellow summer recruit Victor Munoz, but boss Andoni Iraola has offered fans hope he won’t be out for long.



Speaking to Steven Gerrard and TNT Sports after the game, the Spaniard suggested the electrifying winger thought it might be cramp.

Laura Woods noticing Barcola mouthed “cramp” to the manager as he exited the pitch, with the former Bournemouth boss patting him on the back as was replaced.



Iraola said: “I just asked him if it was cramp and he said yes, so that was a relief.

“It was just cramp. We have been rushing Bradley a little bit because he hadn’t played any minutes in pre-season.

“We wanted him to play but said to just give us whatever he had. We have another game in three days.”

Barcola was walking about on the pitch after the game embracing his team-mates and the opposition, seemingly OK.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It capped a frustrating night for the French international after he went clean through on goal and failed to even hit the target.

He dragged the effort wide and many fans might feel for £123m, you have to score those chances.

It was Barcola’s first start for the club after he played the last 26 minutes of their 2-0 victory over Ipswich at the weekend.

But he is clearly still getting up to speed after not doing much of PSG’s pre-season prior to his move.

Iraola seems to be optimistic that it won’t be too bad and to see him walking around the pitch at the end suggests it should not be a bad one.

Sports.title: Chelsea 6 Leeds 3: Cole Palmer climbs off the bench to spark barnstorming comeback in nine-goal Carabao Cup thriller
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS delivered a hat-trick of assists as Xabi Alonso’s cavalry rescued Chelsea from a Carabao Cup nightmare.

Alonso hit the panic button at half-time, with the Blues 1-0 down thanks to goals from Tarik Murahemovic, only for Leeds to score again moments later through Brenden Aaronson.



But his super-subs sparked a comeback, firing four goals in 11 crazy minutes to eventually seal a 5-3 thriller at Stamford Bridge.

Alonso gambled early, starting 16-year-old Reggie Watson – Chelsea’s fourth-youngest player ever – while resting his ‘CPR’ frontline of Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro, and Rogers.



By the break, the Blues were flatlining and desperately needed resuscitation.

Enter Dr. Palmer.



The first half was a tale of two teams, as Leeds looked gritty and ruthless, while Chelsea’s expensive show-ponies were all stepovers and no substance.

Young Blues keeper Mike Penders produced two stunning saves to keep Leeds at bay, but was powerless when £34million defender Murahemovic nodded home Harry Wilson’s deep corner, which left new set piece coach Austin MacPhee practically spitting his words into the Stamford Bridge turf.

Danny Welbeck saw a golden chance blocked by Jaka Bijol before Alonso’s disjointed side trudged down the tunnel to a chorus of groans from players and fans alike.

The Blues were all bark and no bite, until Alonso unleashed the big dogs.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Throwing on Palmer, Rogers, Reece James, and Pedro Neto felt more like a hope and a prayer than a masterstroke from Alonso, but it was a prayer that was answered – with a slight delay…

Ex-Blues academy kid Ethan Ampadu tore down the right early in the second half, feeding Lukas Nmecha to flick past Maxence Lacroix for Brenden Aaronson to tap home.

It felt like game over, until Cole Palmer stepped up to the penalty spot.

Daniel James clumsily felled Pep Chavarria in the box, and Palmer coolly converted the 53rd-minute penalty before wheeling off in celebration with his trademark shivering move.

Just two minutes later, he stroked a silky half-volley into the bottom corner to level the scoring.



Neto fired home a third to complete the turnaround, before Rogers grabbed his treble of assists by teeing up Welbeck to nutmeg new Leeds keeper Michael Zetterer for number four.

Leeds tried to mount a late comeback when Calvert Lewin found the back of the net with 15 minutes to go, but the Blues shut them down once again.

World Cup villain Valentin Barco was already unpopular with the Leeds fans, as he had his every touch booed for his antics in the summer against England.

He left Stamford Bridge popular with the home supporters though, with his 80th-minute strike securing the Blues’ fifth and final goal.

Sports.title: Arsenal ratings: Odegaard’s sensational start to season continues at Napoli but Gyokeres is miles off the pace
Sports.content:
MARTIN ODEGAARD continued his incredible start to the season as he fired Arsenal to a win in their Champions League opener.

The Gunners edged a 1-0 win over Napoli to get their European campaign underway with three points.



Mikel Arteta‘s side dominated the ball and played patient attacking football as they waited for the right moment to pounce.

That came when captain Odegaard let fly from outside the area and broke the deadlock late in the second half.



Odegaard was the star of the show for most of the game, marking his fifth goal contribution in as many games this season.

Here’s how SunSport Arsenal Reporter Joshua Hall rated each individual Arsenal performance…

DAVID RAYA – 7

Uncharacteristically spilled Kevin De Bruyne’s powerful effort in the first half, but was solid with his shot-stopping throughout.

His distribution seems to have gone up another level this season and he was firing the ball to Arsenal shirts at every opportunity.

BEN WHITE – 7

Jurrien Timber travelled with the Arsenal team to Naples, but was still absent from the matchday squad, meaning White will be keeping his starting spot at right-back for a little while longer.

This was another solid performance from the 28-year-old, who isn’t going to be replaced without putting up a fight.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

EZRI KONSA – 8

There was understandably a lot of concern when news of William Saliba‘s back injury spread this summer, but Konsa has stepped into his shoes with ease.

Arteta has spoken in the past about “plug-and-play” signings and Konsa is showing that with his performances already.

This was another top showing from the former Aston Villa man, who looks dominant when he is called into action.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 8

Impressive as ever and adapting really well to playing alongside a new partner in Konsa.



The Brazilian made a crucial intervention to deny Kevin De Bruyne when the Napoli midfielder was bursting into the box.

PIERO HINCAPIE – 6

A first start of the season for the Ecuador international, who has a big task on his hands if he wants to keep in-form Riccardo Calafiori out of the team going forward.

Tried to make his mark with a cross-cum-shot that almost crept in, but was unable to pull off a miraculous goal.

He will be kicking himself for firing a golden opportunity over the bar early in the second half that should have been a guaranteed goal.



DECLAN RICE – 7

Rice has become ‘Mr. Reliable’ for Mikel Arteta ever since his arrival at the club in 2023 – this was another of those commanding performances.

The midfielder was so calm in his own box to prevent Napoli a goal in the first half and offered threat going forward too.

MIKEL MERINO – 7

Always drifting into the box and trying to impact the game like he has done so many times before.

There will be questions about if he should have done better when his first-half header was saved from point blank range.



But perhaps that is a sign of a player starting his first game in months.

MARTIN ODEGAARD – 9

The Norwegian has started the season on fire, using his World Cup campaign as a catalyst for his club form.

This game was no different as his dancing feet and remarkable vision played a part in almost every Arsenal attack.

But after nobody else could finish it off, it was his long-range bullet that found the back of the net and finally rewarded Arsenal for their patient play.



BUKAYO SAKA – 6

Not his usual clinical self despite working into a host of brilliant positions throughout the game.

He will be frustrated with how he made a hash of a huge opportunity when he was played through by Odegaard.

The linesman’s flag spared his blushes despite there being no offside in the build-up.



EBERE EZE – 6

Eze is going to have to play a lot more football on the left flank this season after the departures of Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli.

The England international drifted in and out of the game and struggled to come up with the goods when he did have the ball at his feet.

Ultimately replaced by Christos Tzolis.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 6

Arteta has trusted Kai Havertz in his opening four games this season, but finally gave Gyokeres the nod from the off in Naples.

The striker was largely anonymous, but it is hard to blame him given the way that Napoli set up so deep in their own half.



You have to wonder if Arteta should have stuck to his guns and played Havertz up top, particularly after his masterclass against Chelsea at the weekend.

The German did replace Havertz in the 73rd minute.

SUBSTITUTES

BRUNO GUIMARAES (for Merino, 65 mins) – 7

Another impressive substitute cameo from the Brazilian, who looks hungry to make an impact at Arsenal.



CHRISTOS TZOLIS (for Eze, 65 mins) – 7

Lashed at his chance inside the box as he tried to make an instant impact off the bench.

But managed to register an assist as he made the final pass to Odegaard for the game’s only goal.

NONI MADUEKE (for Saka, 73 mins) – 6

Had to do so much better when he was played through one-on-one against the goalkeeper by Havertz late on.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

KAI HAVERTZ (for Gyokeres, 73 mins) – 7

His technical ability is a level above Gyokeres and it is evident whenever he gets the ball.

Thought he had tucked home a goal of his own in injury time, but was called offside.



MARTIN ZUBIMENDI (for White, 82 mins) – N/A

For the first time since Wimbledon in ​2009, all four top seeds at a Grand Slam have reached the semi-finals, with Sabalenka, Rybakina and Gauff all former major champions and third seed Pegula seeking a maiden Grand Slam title.

Sabalenka has reached the semi-finals here for a sixth consecutive year and is now two wins away from becoming the first woman ‌since Serena Williams from 2012 to 2014 to win three straight titles in New York.

Sports.title: Arteta explains new role for transformed Odegaard
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard is a player transformed at the start of this season - and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta puts his captain's impressive form down to fitness and new positioning.

Odegaard was the match-winner again for Arsenal on Wednesday, thumping in the only goal of the game in the Champions League victory at Napoli.

That hit followed his clinching strike against Chelsea in the Premier League on Sunday and takes his total to four goals in five appearances this season across all competitions.

Odegaard only scored once for Arsenal during an injury-hit 2025/26 campaign but now his stats are up across a range of other attacking metrics, too.

Image: Martin Odegaard is having a much bigger impact in the final third this season

"First of all he needs to be available and last year he missed so many games through injuries," said Arteta when asked in his post-match press conference about Odegaard's improvement.

The Gunners boss also highlighted how fresh combinations with team-mates are playing a part.

"He's got that edge and different relationships around him as well and that helps," said Arteta.

"He can start to go by different heights in the team, especially in the attacking phase, and when we get him into those positions he's a really dangerous player."

That is demonstrated by Odegaard's touches in the opposition box going up from 2.5 per 90 minutes last season to 4.3 per 90 minutes so far this term.

Image: Martin Odegaard produced a starring performance against Napoli

Arteta put Odegaard's freedom to advance into more threatening positions down to the skills of his team-mates in open play, which the Arsenal head coach suggested had been missing previously.

"We have a lot of players that can take the ball there and progress the ball much better than we did in the past," Arteta explained.

"When that happens, [Odegaard] needs to take different heights and angles and positions in order to disorganise the opponent and he's done that really well."

Image: Martin Odegaard's pass map against Napoli shows the areas he operated in

Christos Tzolis is likely to be one of those players Arteta is referencing. The summer signing has four assists to his name already, with three of those coming for Odegaard goals, including the winner in Naples.

But the Arsenal attack down both flanks and through the middle looked extremely dangerous at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Arsenal had 26 shots in total - their most on record (since 2003/04) in the competition. An expected goals total of 4.05 showed they should have got far more for their efforts.

Odegaard, though, did step up and deliver the key moment.

"That's what we need," said Arteta. "The players with the mindset to decide a game and play with personality. To keep taking chances and risks.

"He's getting into those positions much more in recent games and now you feel he has the emotional state that he knows the ball can go in, and he scored an incredible goal tonight."

Odegaard playing with freedom and flair

Analysis by Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

Odegaard is a player in form. That much was clear from early in the game against Napoli. He oozed class and confidence, demanding the ball then finding the gaps in Napoli's defence and threading passes forward. Everything went through him.

His goal, brilliantly taken from the edge of the box after a 29-pass build-up, proved crucial. He now has four in five games this season, a stunning turnaround having only managed one in 36 last term. Odegaard, uninhibited by injuries, looks a different player.

Image: Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring against Napoli

Showing his team-mates how to finish was only one part of his performance. He also ended the game having had more touches, made more passes and created more chances than anyone else on the pitch. Napoli couldn't really get near him.

The scooped pass to release Ben White for the golden chance somehow spurned by Piero Hincapie was one of many examples of his ingenuity against the massed ranks of Napoli players but there were plenty of others. He played with freedom and flair.

"Martin is contributing goals," added Arteta after the game. "That is obviously impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players, to be decisive, and certainly he was that today."

Arsenal continue to feel the benefits.

Sports.title: Chelsea hit SIX second-half goals to see off Leeds in Carabao Cup classic
Sports.content:
An incredible second-half comeback including six goals in 41 minutes saw Chelsea finally blow away Leeds 6-3 in one of the all-time Carabao Cup classics at Stamford Bridge.

The Blues found themselves two goals behind when Brenden Aaronson struck after 47 minutes to add to Tarik Muharemovic's opener, and it appeared Xabi Alonso's first real cup test would end in disappointment - despite the half-time introduction of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers, Pedro Neto and Reece James.

A Palmer penalty turned the game on its head suddenly after Pep Chavarria was caught by Dan James, but it was Rogers who inspired the comeback, making four of Chelsea's six goals.

Three of those assists - for Palmer's second, Neto's strike and the first of two for Danny Welbeck - came as Chelsea netted three times more in 12 minutes, including Welbeck's fourth which should have given them breathing space when he fired through Michael Zetterer's legs.

Not for the first time in Alonso's short reign however, chaos once again reigned over control as Leeds continued to create chances before Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled them back to within a goal with 15 minutes to go.

It was still uncertain that Chelsea had finally sealed their progress when Valentin Barco blasted them 5-3 up from close range from another Rogers assist, but they could finally rest easy in added time - and extinguish Leeds' commendable never-say-die attitude - when Welbeck nodded Barco's wildly mishit effort beyond Zetterer.

If there was ever a goal to sum up a game, this was it. Alonso was handed another clear indication of where his side remain lacking - but for now, chaos isn't serving them too badly.

Farke: No-one was asking for penalty

Leeds head coach Daniel Farke on Sky Sports:

"We played with confidence, there was not even a chance for them, then the referee decided to give a penalty.

"Nobody was asking for it, all of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game."

Alonso: Always a risk making mass changes

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso on Sky Sports:

"There was so many changes. There was a risk. Things weren't going the way we planned, so we had to change. I take responsibility with the first half. The crowd were great, with the atmosphere [pushing the players on].

"I like that [the substitutes] were ready before the game. They knew they weren't starting and they were ready to make an impact.

"When you put together a team that hardly plays together, it is difficult to play at this level when [Leeds] are intense."

Palmer: It's a lot different under Alonso

Player of the match Cole Palmer on Sky Sports:

"You can see I'm enjoying it. Me and Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro, the attacking players.

"Not to say the defenders aren't - but it's a lot different.

"We've still got a bit to go, but we're getting results and that's the main thing."

Sports.title: West Brom win with 10 men at Derby to move top of Championship
Sports.content:
West Brom celebrated a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park after playing for more than an hour with 10 men.

West Brom celebrated a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park after playing for more than an hour with 10 men.

The visitors went in front through Aune Heggebo only to have Brayann Pereira sent off on his debut for a second yellow card.

Pereira could have no complaints about the decision but his side showed determination and character to hold on despite almost constant second-half pressure.

Derby had their moments but created few clear-cut chances with the best falling to striker Lars-Jorgen Salvesen who headed over from eight yards.

There was one nervous moment deep in added time when the visitors survived a huge scramble on the edge of the six-yard box but they held on for a win that takes them top of the Championship table.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brayann Pereira sees red as West Brom go down to 10 against Derby

Derby made a confident start with Sam Szmodics causing problems but it was West Brom who took the lead in the 16th minute against the run of play.

A fast counter opened Derby up and Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipped in a low cross from the left which Heggebo finished at the near post.

After Derby's previous home game ended in defeat to Swansea, it was important they did not concede again and Heggebo headed a decent chance over from eight yards in the 25th minute.

But the visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute after he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor.

Pereira knew it was reckless given the earlier booking and pulled his shirt over his head as he left the pitch.

It opened the door for Derby, who went close in the 43rd minute when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in.

The start of the second half brought more problems for West Brom after Nolan Galves was injured in a challenge and had to be helped off the pitch.

Derby were turning up the heat and should have equalised in the 68th minute but Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward's cross.

That was the best chance Derby had created since the break, which was a testament to the way West Brom had defended under sustained pressure.

There was one last chance for Derby right at the end when Henrik Meister knocked the ball past Max O'Leary but Nat Phillips made a great clearance to sum up a performance full of grit and resolve.

The managers

Derby boss John Eustace:

"Obviously frustrated but I thought we started the game really well and even when we went a goal down I thought the whole of the first half was a real positive from my point of view.

"The lads did exactly what I wanted them to do and we had a couple of chances first half which we couldn't put away.

"Then in the second half West Brom defended really well and I'm disappointed that we couldn't break them down.

"We just need a bit more quality and the lads to step up and take responsibility for trying to make something happen. We got into some really good areas and we've got to keep working in that final third."

West Brom boss James Morrison:

"I thought we were pretty poor for the first 20 or 30 minutes, we caused our own problems really.

"I think the sending off summed up our start really, we gave the ball away far too much and the one time we did string some passes together we scored.

"It was important we got to half time and sorted a few things out. We limited them to crosses coming in and heading from 12 yards, we defended the box really well with everyone putting their bodies on the line.

"That defensive unit of the whole team really when we were low was pretty impressive.

"I felt it from day one really, after last season to now, it's a credit to the lads and the new lads coming in and fitting in really well, hopefully that will spur us on."

Sports.title: Is change needed after Shelton's early-morning finish against Alcaraz?
Sports.content:
The clock ticked to 3.33am local time in New York City when Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz with a clean ace to the delight of thousands of delirious tennis fans still inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, but does something have to be done to stop these early-morning finishes?

Three long matches earlier on Tuesday meant Alcaraz and Shelton did not step on to court until gone 11pm.

The US Open craves its night matches and players love the energy the fans provide - even when a number of matches have already gone past 2am this year.

Sleep schedules, meal times and warm-ups are all impacted by the ticking clock.

"When you finish late, the next day shifts a lot," Aryna Sabalenka said earlier in the tournament. "Like, you still need to get your hours of sleep, so you start later. You just can really mess up your schedule."

Sabalenka is not alone; Venus Williams also said it was "not ideal" that her match against Sofia Kenin last Monday didn't start until past midnight.

"I think it wasn't great for either of us, so I think we both tried our best," she said. "Yeah, I just don't know any other sport where you have to start that late. I definitely think there's room for improvement there."

"But I will say, ultimately, one match a night especially when you get down to the quarter-finals and you know those matches are going to be a lot closer could potentially be the solution.

Sports.title: Odegaard gives dominant Arsenal win over Napoli
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard's superb strike gave Arsenal a deserved 1-0 victory over Napoli in their Champions League opener.

The Gunners should have won by a bigger margin but missed a succession of chances before Odegaard crashed a low shot in off the post from the edge of the box following intricate build-up.

The goal, Odegaard's fourth in five games this season, ensured a winning start for last season's runners-up in this competition but wasteful finishing made it harder than it should have been.

Arsenal attempted 26 shots, their most on record in a Champions League game, worth a whopping 4.05 expected goals but Mikel Merino and Bukayo Saka spurned their best chances of the first half before Piero Hincapie blazed over from close range in the second.

Odegaard's goal, fired in following a quick one-two with substitute Christos Tzolis, finally broke the deadlock but Noni Madueke, another substitute, missed a one-on-one chance with Tzolis's follow-up blocked on the line, leaving Arsenal to suffer a late scare.

Former Manchester City playmaker Kevin De Bruyne appeared well placed to equalise when put through for a rare Napoli chance in the final few minutes, but wasted the chance by opting to cross, ensuring Arsenal could celebrate a victorious start to their European campaign and a fifth straight win of the season in all competitions.

The key moments in Naples

22 SAVE! Eberechi Eze heads a Saka cross back across goal but Merino's header is parried

Eberechi Eze heads a Saka cross back across goal but Merino's header is parried 29: SLICE! Arsenal create another great opening but Saka fails to connect properly with his shot in the centre of the box

Arsenal create another great opening but Saka fails to connect properly with his shot in the centre of the box 45: MISS! Odegaard plays Saka through on goal but he fires wastefully over the bar

Odegaard plays Saka through on goal but he fires wastefully over the bar 50: WASTE! Odegaard lifts the ball over the top to White, whose cross finds Hincapie but the defender somehow blasts over from six yards out

Odegaard lifts the ball over the top to White, whose cross finds Hincapie but the defender somehow blasts over from six yards out 75: AT LAST! Arsenal finally score as a slick passing move ends with Odegaard firing a low shot into the corner

Arsenal finally score as a slick passing move ends with Odegaard firing a low shot into the corner 85 SAVE! Kai Havertz puts Noni Madueke through on the counter but his shot is saved before Tzolis sees his follow-up effort blocked

Kai Havertz puts Noni Madueke through on the counter but his shot is saved before Tzolis sees his follow-up effort blocked 89: SCARE! De Bruyne looks well placed to equalise but chooses to cross instead of shoot and wastes the chance

Odegaard reinvigorated for Arsenal

Analysis by Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

Odegaard is a player in form. That much was clear from early in this game. The Arsenal captain oozed class and confidence, demanding the ball then finding the gaps in Napoli's defence and threading passes forward. Everything went through him.

His goal, brilliantly taken from the edge of the box after a 29-pass build-up, proved crucial. He now has four in five games this season, a stunning turnaround having only managed one in 36 last term. Odegaard, uninhibited by injuries, looks a different player.

But showing his team-mates how to finish was only one part of his performance. He also ended the game having had more touches, made more passes and created more chances than anyone else on the pitch. Napoli couldn't really get near him.

The scooped pass to release Ben White for the golden chance somehow spurned by Piero Hincapie was one of many examples of his ingenuity against the massed ranks of Napoli players but there were plenty of others. He played with freedom and flair.

"Martin is contributing goals," said Mikel Arteta after the game. "That is obviously impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players, to be decisive, and certainly he was that today." Arsenal continue to feel the benefits.

Arteta: We should have scored more

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to TNT Sports:

"Fully deserved for the three points.

"I don't know the amount of chances and situations we generated but the performance doesn't reflect the result. It should have been much bigger - in a really tough environment, a really tough opponent. I think the team was superb.

"The way we competed, attitude, courage, the way we imposed ourselves on the game, the quality we showed to break them down, which is very difficult to do. It was a shame because we missed so many big chances.

"That's great that a lot of very different players got in those situations. Any other day the result [score] would be different."

Yet another clean sheet for Arsenal

Arsenal have won their last 13 group-stage games in the Champions League, the second-longest run in the competition's history after Bayern Munich (17 between December 2020 and November 2023).

Arsenal have kept 20 clean sheets in 40 Champions League games under Mikel Arteta, four more than any other side since the start of 2023/24.

Arsenal's 26 shots against Napoli was their most on record (since 2003/04) in a single Champions League match, while it was also the most Napoli have ever faced in the competition.

There were 29 passes in the build-up to Arsenal's winner, their second-most on record (since 2003/04) for a Champions League goal (33 for Lucas Perez's second at Basel in December 2016).

Sports.title: Gauff to face new world No 1 Rybakina in semis after incredible comeback
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff saved two match points on her way to a three-set victory over teenage French Open winner Mirra Andreeva which set up a semi-final showdown with newly crowned world No 1 Elena Rybakina.

It was a horrible start for 2023 champion Gauff, whose serve and forehand deserted her as she lost the first set in just 26 minutes, hitting only three winners and making 14 unforced errors.

She improved in the second which culminated in a tie-break, during which Russian fifth seed Andreeva squandered two chances to take the match.

That broke Andreeva's spirit and she risked being defaulted after hurling her racket towards her chair, inadvertently sending it spinning towards a camera operator who had to dodge out of the way.

Gauff eventually won 2-6 7-6 (7) 6-2 and revealed she took inspiration from a fellow American's comeback on Tuesday.

"I just had to reset," Gauff said. "I came out at the start, not feeling the ball, giving her too many free points.

"Mirra was playing a great level, but when I went to the restroom after the first set, honestly I was thinking about Frances Tiafoe and how he came back yesterday.

"We all want to do well in front of this crowd. I was trying to leave the court with no regrets, I didn't know what outcome would come. You guys really helped pull me through."

Image: Coco Gauff saved two match points in a stunning fightback against Mirra Andreeva

'Gauff one of few capable of wins like that'

Sky Sports Tennis' Marion Bartoli:

"That was just pure heart to find a way, somehow. It doesn't really matter the level, you just have to find a way on the day.

"She's the one tomorrow in the semi-final of the US Open. If she wins the US Open, no one will remember her level here in the quarters.

"Coco Gauff is one of the only players in the world capable of winning a match like that."

'Difficult defeat to get over for Andreeva'

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman:

"It was amazing to watch, because you've got two brilliant players capable of playing some amazing tennis who through serving issues and errors became so tight and so nervous.

"The ball speed deteriorated, and went down and down. But that's the beauty of tennis. It's about keeping the ball on the island and cutting out unforced errors.

"That is going to be a very difficult defeat for Andreeva to get over, having had match points in the second set. But she will learn so much from it. She'll be incredibly disappointed."

Rybakina claims world No 1 spot after Zheng battle

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the US Open quarter-final between Qinwen Zheng and Elena Rybakina

Earlier, Rybakina clinched the world No 1 spot after beating Qinwen Zheng to book her place in the last four.

The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan will usurp Aryna Sabalenka, whose 99-week reign at the top of the rankings will end on Monday.

Rybakina, the Australian Open champion, has been chasing down Sabalenka all year and will be No 1 for the first time in her career even if the Belarusian goes on to win a third consecutive title.

But Rybakina will have something to say about that as well, having reached the last four at Flushing Meadows for the first time.

Image: Elena Rybakina will officially become the world No 1 on Monday when the rankings refresh

"It's just a number right now, I'm only in the semis and the goal is to win every tournament I play," she said. "I feel like I just need to focus on my game and enjoy tomorrow."

Rybakina dropped a set for the first time this fortnight but hit back strongly in the second.

And Zheng's near-12 hours on court, through three qualifying matches and five in the main draw, finally caught up with her in the decider as Rybakina won 3-6 6-1 6-4.

"It's tough to find words," added Rybakina. "It was a very difficult match, lot's of nerves, maybe not the highest level but I'm glad I pushed through.

"I didn't start that well, I was too negative. It was a lot of unforced errors but I told myself to keep on fighting."

Zheng was enjoying an Emma Raducanu-style run in New York but, although the 23-year-old from China's fairytale eventually came to an end, she is now back on the verge of the top 50 having slipped to 121 after elbow surgery.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tim Henman and Laura Robson share their thoughts on Elena Rybakina becoming the new world No 1 after battling back to beat Qinwen Zheng at the US Open and progress to the semi-finals

'Rybakina showed her class'

Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman:

"It ended up being a really good performance.

"It wasn't the best start from Rybakina, Zheng had something to do with that, but the way she responded in the second and third sets was impressive.

"She was more aggressive from the back of the courts. In that third set, when it was tight, Rybakina really did show her class."

Sports.title: Mac Allister wins it for Liverpool against Atletico on Barcola's eventful full debut
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister's superb strike saw Liverpool come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 at Anfield as Bradley Barcola went off with "cramp" on an eventful home debut.

Barcola was making his first start for Liverpool but felt his calf in the second half and the £123m signing was substituted having missed three good chances to mark the occasion with a goal. It did not impact the result thanks to Mac Allister's rocket.

Marcos Llorente had opened the scoring for the Spanish side with his fifth goal against Liverpool when put through well by Julian Alvarez on the Argentine forward's return to the starting line-up. But that man Dominik Szoboszlai levelled it up before the break.

Image: Dominik Szoboszlai celebrates his equaliser for Liverpool against Atletico Madrid

Curiously, both Liverpool goals came in the immediate aftermath of Barcola chances. Jan Oblak saved to deny him in the build-up to Szoboszlai's goal, Ronald Araujo cleverly recycling the chance. And Mac Allister blasted in to spare his blushes for the second.

Image: Mac Allister scores his side's second goal

Liverpool had drawn their first two Premier League games of the season two apiece, and given the open nature of the game there was a risk of a repeat. But instead Andoni Iraola earned this Anfield victory in his first Champions League match as a head coach.

The key moments from Anfield

1 - CHANCE! Szoboszlai robs Koke but Isak drags his shot wide

15 - SAVE! Barcola chance in behind on the right but Oblak saves

17 - GOAL! Alvarez sends Llorente through and he beats Alisson

27 - SAVE! Alvarez shot from distance tipped just wide by Alisson

30 - SAVE! Wirtz denied by Oblak after starting the move himself

40 - GOAL! Araujo's clever flick puts Szoboszlai in to slot home

49 - WIDE! Wirtz sends Barcola clean through but he shoots wide

50 - GOAL! Mac Allister blasts in left-footed just second later

58 - INJURY! Barcola substituted after going down holding his calf

88 - OFFSIDE! Frimpong sweeps the ball home but is well offside

Iraola finally beats Simeone Andoni Iraola enjoyed his first win over Diego Simeone in his managerial career having failed to win any of his four prior encounters in LaLiga in charge of Rayo Vallecano.

Iraola: Just cramp for Barcola

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola speaking about Bradley Barcola in the press conference:

"No, it's cramp. It's just cramp, there is no injury. With Bradley, it's about building his physical condition.

"We don't really know, or we didn't know until now probably, how much he can play, because he hasn't had any minutes in pre-season for PSG.

"He played 30 the other day. Today we had some question marks, how many minutes he can give us, and probably now we know.

"And I'm very happy because also he has had two very clear chances against the keeper. He hasn't scored, but I want him there. That is where he has to make the difference - arriving to those spots, those positions.

"And I'm very happy because in, I don't know how many minutes he's played, two times against the keeper is a good sign with Bradley."

Image: Barcola's touch map and shot map for Liverpool against Atletico Madrid

Analysis: Barcola's Anfield debut

Sky Sports' Adam Bate at Anfield:

Barcola might have scored twice in the first half on his Anfield bow and missed a big chance at the start of the second but it was still a promising performance. He has been used on the left by Paris Saint-Germain but showed his versatility playing from the right.

Image: Bradley Barcola on his full Liverpool debut against Atletico Madrid at Anfield

His fitness looked sharper than his finishing and it did not take long for him to win over the Kop, his name being chanted inside 15 minutes when he tracked back to shut down an early Atletico counter-attack. That pace looks like it will be a real weapon for Iraola.

The worry was the sight of him trudging off before the hour. The Liverpool boss had stressed the need to manage Barcola given that he had not been involved in pre-season. Iraola needs him up to speed quickly. On this evidence, he can make a difference.

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Alexis Mac Allister makes his point as Liverpool fight back to defeat Atlético
Sports.content:
It was the time and place for Alexis Mac Allister to do his talking on the pitch and the disgruntled Liverpool midfielder delivered on cue. “Very sad” over Liverpool’s refusal to offer him a new contract, while Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch were getting theirs, Mac Allister made Anfield very happy with a match-winning display against Atlético Madrid.

The Argentina international, one of five World Cup finalists involved in an absorbing, delicately-poised contest, vented his frustrations in the best possible and most professional way – from behind an immaculate 20-yard strike into Jan Oblak’s goal rather than a microphone. Mac Allister believes he is playing for a new deal this season and promised to give “100% to my last day” at the pre-match press conference. He was true to his word to extend Atlético’s winless sequence against English opposition in the Champions League league phase to 11 matches.

For Andoni Iraola, it was the perfect start to life as a Champions League coach after an imperfect start to the game. Diego Simeone’s switch to a 3-5-2 formation caught Liverpool cold and it was only when they regrouped in the aftermath of Marcos Llorente’s latest Anfield goal, and again during the half-time interval, that their performance level improved. Mac Allister’s timely moment, Alexander Isak’s relentless industry, Florian Wirtz’s creativity and another performance of drive and intelligence from Szoboszlai ensured the Liverpool head coach had plenty to savour.

“I have to blame myself a bit for the start of the game,” Iraola said. “Atlético surprised us with the way they approached the game. They haven’t used that system too much this season and it’s difficult if you are not ready for it, but we adjusted and played better. In the second half we were the best team. We came back for the third time [this season] and that showed the players are pushing and they have character.”

It was a night of firsts. Iraola coached a Champions League game for the first time in his career – he did take charge of 12 Europa League matches with AEK Larnaca in 2018-19 – Bradley Barcola made his first Liverpool start following a £123m move from Paris Saint-Germain and Julián Álvarez was in Atlético’s starting lineup for the first time this season since his failed attempt to join Barcelona. All appeared to have been forgiven – for now at least – as his name was cheered by the small pocket of Atlético fans when the teams were announced before kick-off and he repaid them by creating the opening goal.

View image in fullscreen Dominik Szoboszlai scores Liverpool’s equaliser late in the first half. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

Llorente was the scourge of Anfield yet again when Álvarez threaded a pass behind the home defence and the right wing-back raced clear on goal. The man who named his dog Anfield after scoring twice to eliminate Jürgen Klopp’s team from the competition in 2020, in the game played while Madrid was in lockdown from the Covid pandemic, lofted a confident finish beyond Alisson. It was Llorente’s fifth goal at Anfield, half of his entire total of Champions League goals. He had been kept onside by Milos Kerkez, who endured a poor night with his positioning and distribution before atoning with a key role in Liverpool’s equaliser.

Álvarez almost doubled the visitors’ lead when granted far too much time and space to take aim from almost 30 yards. Alisson, at full stretch, intervened with a superb finger-tip save. Anfield was growing restless at Liverpool’s carelessness on the ball and Atlético’s comfort on it. But the threat and control from the hosts increased.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wirtz drew a fine save from Oblak at the end of a flowing move involving Barcola and Isak. Liverpool then drew level thanks to tenacity from Kerkez, a lovely touch from Ronald Araújo and Szoboszlai’s instinctive finish. The left-back won possession with a clean, crunching challenge on Lee Kang-in before finding Barcola. The France international was denied a goal on his full debut by Oblak’s low save but Wirtz kept the pressure on and Szoboszlai, having been halted on the edge of the area, got a second bite from Araújo’s clever flick. The midfielder’s first time shot sailed into the far corner.

Barcola should have put Liverpool ahead when played through on goal by Wirtz early in the second half. The winger had time to measure the finish but pulled it wide of Oblak’s right-hand post. He would later depart with cramp. Liverpool were ahead one minute later when the lively Rio Ngumoha beat Llorente and his cross fell to Mac Allister via a deflection off Isak. Mac Allister told Szoboszlai to leave the ball and drilled home an unstoppable left-footed drive from 20 yards. Atlético remained dangerous and the introduction of Ademola Lookman added an extra dimension to the visitors’ attack but Liverpool defended impressively to secure a deserved victory.

Sports.title: Ødegaard ‘edge’ delights Arteta as Arsenal secure narrow win at Napoli
Sports.content:
After their record-breaking feats last year in the Champions League, Arsenal are at it again. But having been delayed along with hundreds of travelling supporters by travel chaos on Tuesday, Mikel Arteta’s side had to bide their time against Napoli until Martin Ødegaard continued his rich vein of goalscoring with the crucial strike 15 minutes from full time.

Perhaps it was the fact that, at Uefa’s insistence, they were forced to wear red shorts for the first time since a Premier League game against Watford in 2022 that Arsenal were not quite at their flowing best here and missed a hatful of chances.

Yet they were deserved winners in the end and the substitute Noni Madueke should have made the ­victory more comprehensive late on.

Having come so close to breaking their duck in this competition last year after becoming the first team to win all eight of their league stage matches, Arsenal look capable of going one better this time if Ødegaard can keep up this sparkling form.

He now has four goals in his last five games after scoring once in all competitions last year and it was the Norway captain whose name was being chanted by the fans who were kept behind more than an hour after the final whistle.

“That’s what we need – players with that mindset to decide the game and to play with that personality,” said Arteta. “He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games and I feel he has this emotional state that he knows that the ball can go in. He’s got that edge and he’s now got different relationships around him [in the team] as well. That helps.”

Arteta has bad memories of this stadium after being sent off in a 2-0 defeat during the Champions League group stage in 2013. But Arsenal’s most recent match here ended in victory as they qualified for the Europa League semi-finals under Unai Emery in 2019. Both clubs have been crowned domestic champions since then, with Napoli ending their 33-year wait in 2023 then doing it again two years later. Yet Champions League success has continued to elude them after finishing 30th in the league phase last season.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta talks with Kevin De Bruyne, the former Manchester City midfielder, after the match. Photograph: Ciro De Luca/Reuters

That was in stark contrast to Arsenal, who were unbeaten over 14 matches before falling at the final hurdle. It was telling that Arteta kept faith with four of his back five that started against Chelsea on Sunday, with Piero Hincapié replacing Riccardo Calafiori at left-back but failing to match the Italian’s finishing ability with one glaring miss. Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyökeres also made their first starts of the season but largely disappointed, with the Sweden striker making way for Kai Havertz just before Ødegaard’s winner.

Those Arsenal supporters that did make it to southern Italy had no problem making themselves heard throughout, with plenty of empty seats in the home sections despite Max Allegri’s attempts to rally Napoli’s fans beforehand. The game quickly settled into a pattern as the visitors set up camp in Napoli’s half and the hosts attempted to hit them on the break. Kevin De Bruyne – no stranger to facing Arsenal after a decade in the sky blue of Manchester City – forced David Raya into a rare mistake after a typically driving run through the midfield but the ball was scrambled away to safety.

That came just after a spectacular overhead kick from Bukayo Saka at the other end had been saved by Alex Meret. Merino should have scored when he was set up by Eze’s clever header across the face of goal before Ben White drilled a shot straight into Meret’s grateful gloves.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Matteo Politano managed to test Raya again as Napoli continued to find gaps in Arsenal’s normally watertight defence. Saka blazed over after a brilliant through ball from Ødegaard on the stroke of half-time, with replays confirming the assistant had been wrong to raise his flag.

View image in fullscreen Martin Ødegaard scores the only goal of the match at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

Meret did not return for the second half and was replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, once on Manchester United’s books. The Serbia goalkeeper was a mere spectator for a flowing Arsenal move featuring a sumptuous scooped pass into the area that ended with Hincapié missing the target after being picked out at the far post by Ben White’s header. Suddenly Napoli found themselves suffocated by a blanket of red. Allegri, who knows what it feels like to have lost in a Champions League final after suffering that fate twice in three years at Juventus, responded by switching to a back five and trying to hang on.

Arsenal’s pressure eventually told when another substitute, Christos Tzolis, exchanged passes with White and teed up Ødegaard, whose shot flew in off the post despite Milinkovic-Savic just getting his fingertips to the ball. Havertz had a goal disallowed for offside in injury time, but the mission was already complete.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer powers Chelsea to comeback win over Leeds in nine-goal epic
Sports.content:
Where’s the fun in doing it the easy way? Chelsea remain chaotic at the back but can drag their opponents into horrible places. It helps, mind you, to have some assistance from the referee. Jarred Gillett and Cole Palmer? They made for a killer ­combination as Chelsea swerved embarrassment and treated Stamford Bridge to one of life’s rarities: a classic in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

Gillett, a referee who always seems to be guessing when he makes key calls, was the villain as far as Leeds were concerned. They had just gone 2-0 up when Gillett altered the flow of the tie by pointing to the spot after Pep Chavarría made the most of slight contact from Daniel James. The subsequent conversion from Palmer was inevitable and from there so was the comeback from Chelsea, who rattled through four goals in 12 minutes before eventually reaching the last 16 by winning 6-3.

It made little sense. It could have gone down as Xabi Alonso’s first ­misjudgment as Chelsea’s manager. The Carabao Cup is important given the Spaniard’s side are not in Europe, but his rotation almost backfired. Chelsea were shambolic after making nine changes – the 16-year-old debutant Reggie Watson was overrun in midfield while Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens struggled in attack – and Alonso was in emergency mode when he made a quadruple change at half-time.

“I take responsibility,” Alonso said. “No player is to blame. It’s the ­decisions we took. When you don’t have this time to work with them, it’s difficult to compete at this level. I need to take my own blame for the things that happen. I need to be able to help them better. They are not responsible. After you need to react and think what’s better for the team.”

Quick Guide Championship: Ten-man West Brom win at Derby to go top Show West Bromwich Albion held on for a memorable 1-0 victory over Derby at Pride Park, after playing for more than an hour with 10 men. Aune Heggebø's early goal proved enough to take the Baggies top of the table, despite Brayann Pereira being dismissed on his debut after collecting two first-half yellow cards. Derby had started the stronger, but West Brom swept downfield to score in the 16th minute, Jimmy-Jay Morgan whipping in a low cross from the left which Heggebø [pictured] finished at the near post. The visitors were rocked by the dismissal of Pereira in the 34th minute, as he was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge on Charlie Taylor. The hosts went close just before half-time when David Ozoh flashed a low ball across the six-yard box with no white shirt able to turn it in. Derby should have levelled in the 68th minute but Lars-Jørgen Salvesen headed over from Joe Ward’s cross. Late on, Nat Phillips made a great clearance after a late goalmouth scramble, summing up a performance full of grit and resolve. James Morrison's side move above West Ham to top the Championship table with 13 points from six games. Either Charlton or QPR could have joined them on 13 points, but the sides played out a stalemate at the Valley. Derby, meanwhile, slipped into the bottom three with their fourth defeat in six games. Norwich moved up to ninth in the table as they edged past visitors Birmingham 2-1 to make it three wins in four league games. Oscar Schwartau's screamer opened the scoring, the young Dane lashing an unstoppable right-footed drive past James Beadle from 25 yards out. Papa Diallo's first goal for the Canaries doubled their advantage before the break, as the Senegal winger sidefooted home from Andre Brooks' cross. Carlos Vicente pulled a goal back for the visitors, but wasted a glorious chance to equalise near the end as Chris Davies’ men suffered their first league defeat this season. Press Association Photograph: Morgan Harlow/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Equally Alonso can take credit for responding. His moves were decisive. Reece James offered security after replacing Watson and Pedro Neto scored after coming on for Malo Gusto, who could barely complete a pass during a wretched first half. Leeds, beaten at this stage for the 14th time in 18 years, were overwhelmed once their lead was halved. Morgan Rogers and Palmer were devastating after replacing Estêvão and Gittens. Rogers had a hand in four goals and Palmer, who scored twice, seemed affronted by the notion of Leeds going through.

It finished as another thrilling attacking display from Chelsea, who have scored 16 goals in Alonso’s first five games. There are flaws to fix at the other end, though. Leeds also experimented, Daniel Farke making eight changes, but controlled the first half. They led when the Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-back Tarik Muharemovic, signed from Sassuolo last summer, headed Harry Wilson’s corner past Mike Penders in the 23rd minute.

Chelsea have already conceded 10 goals in all competitions. Leeds could have doubled their lead through Sean Longstaff. Valentín Barco and ­Watson, son of the former Wigan ­midfielder Ben Watson, were second best in midfield.

Leeds were on their way when Barco lost possession three minutes into the second half. Ethan Ampadu charged past Rogers and found Lukas Nmecha, who teed up Brenden ­Aaronson to make it 2-0.
