View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto fires home Chelsea’s third goal at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Chelsea needed a lift. Chavarría crossed from the left and went to ground. Gillett whistled and Palmer scored with 53 minutes played. “He gave out of nothing a penalty where it wasn’t even a chance for them,” Farke said. “A quality player scores and the body language of the Chelsea players was different.”

Palmer was in his element, equalising in the 55th minute after Rogers laid the ball off for his pal to stroke a casual finish past Michael Zetterer from 20 yards. Chelsea were rampant and led on the hour, Palmer and Rogers combining for Neto to finish well. Leeds looked dizzy. They readied the changes but Danny Welbeck made it 4-2 with a sharp turn and finish in the 65th minute.

Leeds kept fighting. Dominic Calvert-Lewin came on and pulled one back to remind Alonso of Chelsea’s defensive weaknesses. Chelsea responded, Rogers crossing for Barco to score his first goal for the club. The sixth followed, Barco’s mis-hit shot diverted in by Welbeck. “A crazy nuts game,” Farke said. That’s been the way for Chelsea under Alonso.

Sports.title: Infantino installs loyalist to oversee Caribbean as he splits Fifa management
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has separated Fifa’s management of the Caribbean countries from the rest of Concacaf in a move widely regarded by his opponents as an attempt to split the alliance to remove him from office.

Concacaf covers North and Central America as well as the Caribbean and was previously managed as one bloc. But the Guardian has learned that the former Switzerland midfielder Gelson Fernandes, an Infantino loyalist, has been appointed as the director of member associations for the Caribbean, in addition to his position looking after Fifa’s African members.

Fernandes, who played for Manchester City, Leicester and eight other clubs, joined Fifa in 2022 as director of member associations for Africa and was promoted two years later to become deputy chief members associations officer globally.

The 40-year-old works closely with Fifa’s chief members associations officer, Elkhan Mammadov, a close ally of Infantino described by many national associations as the president’s key enforcer.

Fernandes has replaced Jair Bertoni as Fifa’s liaison with the 21 Caribbean-based members, with the national associations and Concacaf informed of the change last week without consultation.

In a statement Fifa confirmed the appointment, which it said was designed to support Infantino’s vision of making the sport truly global.

“Fifa can confirm that Gelson Fernandes has taken on responsibility for the Caribbean region, in addition to his current role as regional director Africa,” it said. “With his extensive experience at Fifa and strong knowledge of football development programmes, Gelson will lead the regional team and will work closely with the member associations across the Caribbean to further support the development of football in their respective countries, following the Fifa president’s vision: making football truly global.”

Concacaf is attempting with Uefa and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to oust Infantino. Sources at several member associations in Europe and North America regard the change as an attempt to split the Concacaf vote before March’s presidential election, with one characterising it as “an administrative war” against its president, Victor Montagliani.

The Canadian is viewed by many in Uefa as the most credible candidate to beat Infantino, although Montagliani has yet to decide whether to stand and is committed to seeking re-election as Concacaf’s president.

Infantino has stepped up his re-election campaign in the aftermath of the World Cup sell-off scandal, ignoring a written request from Montagliani to stay away from a meeting of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU) in the Dominican Republic last month.

As revealed by the Guardian, Infantino used the CFU meeting to announce approval for numerous Fifa-funded development projects for the region worth millions of dollars in what some observers described as an attempt to lobby for votes.

Mexico has split from Concacaf by announcing its support for Infantino, and losing the backing of the Caribbean would be a significant setback for those pushing to remove Infantino.

There have been some early signs that Infantino’s tactics are paying off, with the president of the Jamaican federation, Michael Ricketts, this week backing the status quo and comparing Uefa to spoiled children.

“Infantino might have made a mistake, but the intentions were to help Caribbean countries or help smaller countries,” Rickets told the Jamaica Observer. “Can you imagine Jamaica getting $40m to invest in football? Can you imagine the difference that would make in four or five years?

“I am not supporting Uefa because I think that they always want to be in opposition and always want to oppose. It doesn’t matter who is president, they are going to have issues. It doesn’t matter how well the president does, they are going to have issues and I think that Uefa is behaving like a set of spoilt kids.”

Uefa’s 55 members are believed to be united but the strength of the AFC alliance is unclear, with Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates having defied the confederation by endorsing Infantino.

Infantino last weekend reaffirmed his intention to seek re-election for a fourth term. The deadline for other candidates seeking to stand is 18 November.

Sports.title: Scottish roundup: Miovski hits last-gasp Rangers winner and Celtic keep 100% record
Sports.content:
A dramatic last-gasp strike from substitute Bojan Miovski gave Rangers a 1-0 Premiership win over St Mirren at Ibrox.

Back in the technical area after a two-game touchline suspension, Derek McInnes watched St Mirren’s Australian goalkeeper Jacob Chapman keep the home side at bay in the first half with a string of saves, albeit helped by some poor finishing.

Craig McLeish’s side, who lost 5-1 at Ibrox in the Premier Sports Cup last month, grew in confidence after the break and Fraser Taylor missed a great chance while the frustrated home support returned to the state of agitation which characterised the start of the season.

However, in the final seconds of normal time, Miovski, on for Djeidi Gassama, pounced in the box to grab the winner to make it four victories in a row.

Summer signing Mika Baur notched his first goal for Celtic as the Scottish champions maintained their perfect start to their title defence with a 1-0 victory away to St Johnstone.

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s Mika Baur scored his first Celtic goal at McDiarmid Park. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

The German midfielder struck from close range early in the second half after the debutant Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone had produced a stunning first-half save to deny Saints midfielder Joel Cotterill.

It was a night when the Celtic head coach, Martin O’Neill, was able to demonstrate the depth of his squad before Sunday’s Old Firm meeting away to Rangers in the Premier Sports Cup, with key players such as Camilo Duran, Benjamin Nygren and Kieran Tierney on the bench and defender Cameron Carter-Vickers given the evening off.

Although far from their convincing best, the Hoops did enough to close out a sixth consecutive league victory this term and their 13th in a row in total stretching back to the closing weeks of last season.

Sports.title: Rosario ‘grabbed my bottom’ during Manchester City’s win at Porto, claims Haaland
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland has claimed Pablo Rosario “grabbed my bottom” during Manchester City’s 2-0 win at Porto on Tuesday. The incident occurred in the 92nd minute, with Haaland having scored City’s goals. The forward and midfielder grappled, went to ground and were booked after being separated.

“I was really keen on a hat-trick and it seemed like he was very eager to stop me from getting it,” Haaland told Norway’s TV 2. “It was a little interesting, that – you’ll be seeing a picture where he’s grabbing my bottom. It’ll be interesting to see that picture.”

The flashpoint followed one as half-time neared in a niggly encounter. After Marc Guéhi and Gabriel Veiga had a coming together that left the latter with a head injury, tempers frayed. When the teams walked off for the interval a bust-up occurred involving players and staff near the tunnel.

Images showed Rúben Dias placing a hand on what appeared to be Francesco Farioli, the Porto head coach. Uefa will wait for the match report of the referee, Szymon Marciniak, and its delegate, Stéphanie Ford, before deciding whether to bring any action against the defender or City.

Haaland’s 47th-minute opener was a header and the No 9 revealed he had been working on the skill recently with his dad, Alf Inge, a former City player.

“Two days ago I was practising headers with my dad in the garden,” he said. “Over the years, I’ve worked a lot on my heading. I’ve improved it massively and it’s become a strength of my game. I think a lot of it comes down to experience.”

Haaland concurred with his manager, Enzo Maresca, that he may need a break soon. “It’s not easy to get any rest in this business,” the 26-year-old said.

“Like during the international break, we play four games in 10 or 11 days, so it’s not easy. But you have to try to squeeze in a few days here and there and give your mind a bit of a break.”

Sports.title: Champions League roundup: Raphinha shines as Barcelona thrash Feyenoord
Sports.content:
Raphinha let his goals do the talking after being omitted from the Ballon d’Or shortlist, striking twice as Barcelona eased to a 5-1 win over Feyenoord in the Champions League.

The Brazilian was a surprise omission from this week’s 30-strong list of candidates for the prestigious award but brushed any disappointment aside to continue his early season hot streak at a rain-soaked Camp Nou. The forward finished brilliantly in the third minute and added a second just before the hour mark to down the Eredivisie side and take his tally to eight goals in six outings at the start of the campaign.

The summer signing Karim Adeyemi produced a stunning finish, Lamine Yamal stroked a free-kick through a gap in the Dutch wall and recent arrival Gabriel Jesus opened his account for the club just two minutes after stepping off the bench.

There was little to celebrate for Giovanni van Bronckhorst on his Barça return but Sem Steijn gave the visiting fans something to enjoy when he poked in at far post late on.

“The most important thing is we are playing like a team, like one unit,” the Barcelona head coach, Hansi Flick, said. “We controlled the game, we are dominant and this is fantastic to see. This is our style and how we want to play.”

Ferran Torres scored a hat-trick and Ousmane Dembélé also starred as Paris Saint-Germain began their quest to win a third successive Champions League title by thrashing Slovan Bratislava 6-1 at the Parc des Princes.

View image in fullscreen Paris Saint-Germain’s Ferran Torres celebrates scoring their fifth goal with Ousmane Dembélé. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters

Last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Dembélé had scored twice by the midway point of the first half in the French capital, and then set up Spain’s World Cup final hero Torres to make it 3-0 by the interval.

Torres, a close-season signing from Barcelona, added two more just after the restart to complete his hat-trick before the hour mark, with Suleiman Camara pulling one back for the Slovakian champions and Fabián Ruiz then sealing PSG’s win.

Elsewhere, Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic struck a 12-minute first-half hat-trick to ⁠earn ⁠a ​3-1 victory over Viking Stavanger.

He opened the ​scoring after 20 minutes with a touch at the near post, but Viking, making their first appearance in the league phase of the Champions League, were level two minutes later when Zlatko Tripic finished a ⁠swift counter-attack with his left foot.

Sports.title: Carrick up for ‘magical’ Champions League but derby timing ‘not ideal’
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick is excited to lead Manchester United on their return to the “magical” Champions League but admitted playing on Thursday night was “not ideal” with the derby on Sunday.

United welcome Sabah to Old Trafford after a two-year Champions League absence. The Azerbaijani club are making their debut among Europe’s elite, having been in existence for less than a decade.

“It’s a magical competition,” Carrick, who won the competition in 2008 with United, said. “It’s where we all want to be. When you’re out of it, you realise how special it is, and when you’re in it, you want to make the most of it. I think we’ve all seen some special, special nights and felt some special things in this competition over the years.

“It’s where we want to be, it’s what we want to get back to, and it’s the best competition to challenge yourself and to push against the best. We’re delighted to be here, but we’re not here to just enjoy the occasion. We’re here to do business and go as far as we possibly can.

“To win the Champions League for me was the ultimate and was the best feeling I’ve had. Be nice some day to feel that again.”

United have made a mixed start to their Premier League campaign, picking up four points from three games, and this will be a testing period for a club that played just 40 games last season. If United reach the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup, they will not have a free midweek until mid-January.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick won the Champions League in 2008 against Chelsea in Moscow. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

Manchester City visit Old Trafford on Sunday and will have an extra two days to recover from their game at Porto on Tuesday. “I’m not concerned,” Carrick said of the turnaround.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I wouldn’t say it’s ideal in some ways, but it’s not something that we’ve given too much thought about. We’re not in control of that. We’ve got to deal with the cards that we’re dealt and that’s what it is, so we’ll make the most of it.”

United’s only senior left-back, Luke Shaw, did not train on Wednesday after being given a further day of rest. “We’ll see by tomorrow how he is, but it’s not an ongoing thing or a plan,” Carrick said.

Sports.title: ‘That is criminal’ – Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer have hilarious argument after Man-of-the-Match prize awarded
Sports.content:
‘That is criminal’ – Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer have hilarious argument after Man-of-the-Match prize awarded

Morgan Rogers couldn't believe that he didn't get awarded Man of the Match after Chelsea's 6-3 win over Leeds United in the Carabao Cup.

The Blues were trailing 1-0 at half time in their delayed game before Xabi Alonso introduced Rogers, Cole Palmer and Pedro Neto at half time to totally flip the game.



5 In the end, it turned into a great night for Chelsea Credit: Getty

Palmer scored twice and Rogers grabbed FOUR assists, but it was the former who claimed the Man of the Match award.

This led to a pretty hilarious argument live on Sky Sports between the pair.

It started with Rogers, who said: "Mate, I got four assists! Nah, nah, I can't believe that. That is mental. He scored a penalty. That is mental."



Palmer then said: "I started the comeback. But I'll say you should have had it."

To which Rogers responded: "Don't mention me. I am just a bystander. That is criminal."



Rogers robbed

There is no question that both players had a huge impact on the game even if it wasn't immediate.

That is because Leeds doubled their lead early in the second half through Brenden Aaronson.



They had opened the scoring through Tarik Muharemovic's towering header and were good value for it.

But Dan James' foul on Pep Chavarria in the Leeds box changed everything.

5 Rogers was left absolutely stunned that he didn't pick up Man of the Match Credit: Sky Sports

5 The duo's banter and off-field relationship appears to be helping on the pitch as well



Palmer stepped up to score a penalty, and he bagged the equaliser soon after.

Reece James hurled a throw-in into the box that Rogers flicked into Palmer's path.

The England international wrapped his left boot around it and sent it into the far corner.

It was soon 3-2 with Rogers grabbing his second assist after Palmer had played a pass to him.



The pass wasn't quite perfect, so the former Aston Villa man lunged at the ball.

He won the 50/50 and sent it through for Neto, who struck a lovely first-time strike off the inside of the far post.

The hat-trick of assists came for Rogers as he dribbled down the right and played a low ball into the box.

5 Palmer began the Chelsea fightback, scoring two of their six goals Credit: Getty



Danny Welbeck controlled, turned and fired it home via a slight deflection.

There is definitely the argument to suggest the fourth assist for Rogers might not actually be his.

He drilled a low cross in that deflected to Valentin Barco, who lashed home from close range.

But even if it doesn't go down as his, he still definitely got a hat-trick of assists.



Alonso's thoughts

It has been an exciting start to life for Alonso at Chelsea with his side scoring and conceding plenty of goals.

And he admitted after the game that he got his team selection wrong with nine changes from the defeat to Arsenal.

5 Alonso's men have been the great entertainers this season, scoring 16 goals in five matches in all competitions so far Credit: Getty

He said: "Yeah, there was so many changes. There was a risk.

"Things weren't going the way we planned, so we had to change (at half-time). I take responsibility with the first half.



"They knew they weren't starting and they were ready to make an impact. I'm happy with the result and the reaction."

But he is pleased to see Palmer and Rogers linking up so nicely, adding: "For sure, it's so important. To have a great chemistry between them. They enjoy assisting together. It's important for the team."

Sports.title: Liverpool fans in stitches at Steven Gerrard’s brutal jibe after Marcos Llorente Anfield pet dog name claim
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans in stitches at Steven Gerrard’s brutal jibe after Marcos Llorente Anfield pet dog name claim

Steven Gerrard fired a brutal dig at Everton after Marcos Llorente opened the scoring for Atletico Madrid against Liverpool.

The Reds legend was on co-commentary for TNT Sports as his former side fought back to clinch a 2-1 win in their Champions League opener at Anfield.

5 Alexis Mac Allister was the match-winner for Liverpool against Atletico Madrid Credit: Getty

Goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister gave the Premier League side a hard fought victory in Andoni Iraola's first-ever match in the European competition.

Quick-witted Gerrard

Liverpool survived an early scare in the clash, as Atletico took an early lead when Marcos Llorente slotted home on 17 minutes.

This saw the Spaniard keep up his incredible goalscoring record against the Reds, netting five goals in as many games at Anfield.

Llorente's exploits have caught the eye over the years, with midfielder famously naming his dog Anfield after Atletico knocked Liverpool out of the Champions League in 2020.

It didn't take long for this to be brought up on commentary during Wednesday night's clash, with TNT commentator Darren Fletcher reminding viewers of the trivia.

On Llorente, Fletcher said: "He actually has a dog called Anfield, based on the fact that he's scored so many goals here."

And co-commentator Gerrard left Liverpool fans delighted with his quick-witted response, as he quipped: "Might call mine Goodison."

Everton supporters won't have enjoyed the brutal dig, as the Reds icon reminded them of his Merseyside derby heroics as a player.

Goodison Park was of course the Toffees' home ground before they moved into Hill Dickinson Stadium in the 2025/26 season.

Gerrard certainly enjoyed facing off against his local rivals, scoring ten goals in Merseyside derbies in his Liverpool career.

5

5 Gerrard was quick to remind Everton fans of his dominance at Goodison Park as a player Credit: Getty

The Premier League icon's goalscoring record puts him fourth in the all-time goalscoring ranks for the fixture, with only Sandy Young, Dixie Dean and Ian Rush scoring more.

And Goodison Park proved a happy hunting ground for Gerrard, who won 16 of his 18 games at the stadium, scoring twice along the way.

It was a joke appreciated by supporters on the red half of Merseyside, with one saying on X: "Gerrard saying he'll name his dog Goodison hahahhahaha."

Another added: "Yerrrrs Stevie Lad."

While this fan cheekily said: "Well, at least Everton got mentioned on a champions league night. I’d say that’s a successful night for them haha."

And this Liverpool fan said: "Haha my captain!!"

Liverpool edge past Atletico

5 Liverpool's current No.8 in Szoboszlai started Liverpool's comeback Credit: Getty

5 This was Liverpool's most complete performance under Iraola so far Credit: Getty

Gerrard delighted Liverpool fans with a cheeky dig at Everton midway through Liverpool's hard fought win, the Reds faithful will have been even happier with how things ended up at Anfield.

After Llorente's opener, Szoboszlai equalised for Iraola's side on 40 minutes, stroking home after a delightful flick from Ronaldo Aruajo.

And the comeback was complete minutes into the second half, as Mac Allister fired Liverpool in front.

The midfielder, who recently confirmed Liverpool did not intend to offer him a new contract, let rip with a thunderous strike from just outside the box to put the hosts 2-1 up.

This proved enough to seal victory for the Reds, though the result wasn't completely stress free.

£123million summer arrival Bradley Barcola sparked concerns when he limped off just before the hour mark, but head coach Iraola later reassured fans that this was due to cramp.

Sports.title: Arsenal labelled the ‘best team in Europe’ as Martin Odegaard masterclass inspires huge win
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea defender Scott Minto hailed Arsenal as 'the best team in Europe' following a dominant display against Napoli.

A thunderous second-half strike from captain Martin Odegaard proved to be the difference on a sweltering Champions League night in Naples.



3 Three of Odegaard's six Champions League goals have come from outside the box Credit: AFP

The Norwegian let rip with a first-time effort from just outside the 18-yard box that fizzed away from Napoli goalkeeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, capping off a fine move from the Gunners that featured plenty of neat interplay.

The stats behind Martin Odegaard's performance

Odegaard's goal - his first in the Champions League since March 2025 - was the cherry on top of what was a true captain's display.

He was at the centre of everything good for the Gunners as he created the most chances (6), had the most touches (20) and completed the most passes that broke Napoli's defensive line (5) throughout the contest.



But it wasn't just a one-man show from Odegaard, as the entire Arsenal squad combined to repel a Napoli attack that often looked to strike in transitional play.

Crucially, it was another clean sheet for Mikel Arteta's side, who have now kept 20 in their last 40 Champions League fixtures.



What did Scott Minto say about Arsenal's performance against Napoli?

And for Minto, who was on commentary for talkSPORT, he could only wax lyrical about Arsenal's all-round display.

"It's almost as if Arsenal fans are wanting to be in May really, because they are peaking right now," Minto said.



"I think they are the best team in Europe. They look the most complete team.

"There were times in the first half where they did look un-Arsenal-like, where they on the transition were quite open.

"But still David Raya didn't have too many saves to make. One in particular from Matteo Politano and Kevin De Bruyne. And that's about it really.

3 Arsenal's win over Napoli preserved their 100 per cent win rate this season Credit: Getty



"And in the second half, they just absolutely stepped it up and led by their captain, their talisman.

"And when he plays and plays well, they're a special side. No one can complain… the little one-twos, it's like a conductor in an orchestra dictating the tempo and the pace of the music you're about to sit back and enjoy. He's a wonderful player, it's a wonderful strike.

"And really, if anything, the scoreline flatters Napoli."

How does Martin Odegaard's goal tally this season compare to other seasons?

Odegaard's winner against Napoli continued his dream start to the campaign as he took his goal tally to four.

He got on the scoresheet in Arsenal's 3-0 rout of Manchester City to win the Community Shield before he netted the club's third of the Premier League season in a dominant opening day win over Coventry City.



Odegaard then proved to be the hero for the Gunners in a pulsating 2-1 win over Chelsea last Sunday.

3 Odegaard's goal against Napoli was his 46th for Arsenal Credit: Getty

Impressively, he has comfortably surpassed his goal haul for the entirety of the 2025/26 campaign, in which he scored just once.

And he is now well on track to beat his tally from the 2024/25 season, where he netted six times in all competitions.



Odegaard now switches his attention back to the Premier League, with the Gunners next in action away to Sunderland on Saturday at 8pm

Sports.title: Barcelona stadium is the new Old Trafford despite £1.3bn renovation as press box drenched after biblical downpour
Sports.content:
Barcelona stadium is the new Old Trafford despite £1.3bn renovation as press box drenched after biblical downpour

The press boss at Barcelona's newly renovated Nou Camp was drenched by torrential rain during their recent Champions League win.

Barca kicked off their European campaign with an emphatic 5-1 win over Feyenoord in their first league phase game on Wednesday.



4 Raphinha scored his third goal in his last two games against Feyenoord Credit: AFP

A Raphinha double sandwiched between goals from Karim Adeyemi and Lamine Yamal put Hansi Flick's side in cruise control, before new signing Gabriel Jesus opened his Barcelona account late on.

Camp Nou issues laid bare

Barca stormed to victory on a rainy night at the Camp Nou, and some inside the ground ended up even more soaked than the players.

With torrential rain striking in Catalonia, footage shared online has shown the stadium's press box being drenched by the conditions.



Barcelona's iconic home has been in the process of a £1.3billion renovation project since 2023, with Barca only returning to play at the stadium in November 2025 after two years away.

However, certain parts of the venue are still being refurbished, as journalists inside the ground discovered on Wednesday night.



One video has been shared on social media showing a stream of water falling through an opening onto the press box.

Rain is seen pouring down onto the reporters' desk, with water lashing off the table and flooding the surface.



One journalist is shown retrieving an item from the puddle of water on the table, with the conditions making it impossible for journalists to work on their laptops.

Scaffolding can be seen in the press box, making it likely that reconstruction work is ongoing in this part of the Camp Nou.

Barcelona's home ground isn't the only venue to succumb to the elements.

4 Fans braved torrential conditions at the Nou Camp to watch Barcelona thump Feyenoord Credit: AFP



4 Manchester United's Old Trafford has experienced similar roof leaks in recent years

In recent years, Manchester United's Old Trafford home has experienced similar problems, with fans being drenched on more than one occasion as the stadium roof failed to contain the rain.

Is the Camp Nou renovation complete?

The recent Camp Nou footage comes after Barcelona reportedly ran out of money during their £1.3billion stadium renovation.

Work on the venue began after the 2022/23 season, with the Catalan giants eventually returning in November last year.



They played at the 55,000-seater Olympic Stadium on the city's Montjuic hill during most of the construction.

But significant work is still required as the club plans to increase the Nou Camp’s capacity to an incredible 105,000.

Heavy construction is ongoing on the stadium’s upper tier, with Barcelona currently only able to play in front of a reduced 62,000 capacity.

4 Barcelona's Camp Nou is one of the most impressive stadiums in Europe Credit: Getty



Additionally, the final stage is the refurbishment of the roof, with venue's shortcomings in this area plain to see in Barca's last match.

The La Liga champions have requested to use the Estadi Olimpic Lluis Companys as a temporary home for the 2027/28 campaign.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola injury as Liverpool fans hold breath on £123m man
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola injury as Liverpool fans hold breath on £123m man

Andoni Iraola has assured Liverpool fans that Bradley Barcola coming off during their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid was just a bout of cramp.

The French winger, who joined the Reds for an initial £106million rising to £123m this summer, went down just before the hour mark in the Champions League clash at Anfield on Wednesday night.

4 Barcola's issue is not as bad as first feared Credit: TNT Sports

Barcola appeared in some discomfort and rubbed his left calf while receiving medical treatment.

He was then substituted, with Jeremie Frimpong coming on in his place.

Andoni Iraola provides update on Bradley Barcola injury

However, in a major boost, Reds boss Iraola insisted there was no serious issue with Barcola.

"It's just cramps, especially with Bradley," Iraola said.

"We are kind of rushing him as we haven't had him in pre-season."

The Champions League fixture marked Barcola's first start for Liverpool, having made his Premier League debut courtesy of a 26-minute cameo off the bench last Friday against Ipswich Town.

Barcola's injury came just minutes after he missed a golden chance to put Liverpool in the lead.

The French flyer was slipped in via a perfect through-ball from Florian Wirtz and raced clear towards goal, but he fired his effort wide of the post.

Luckily for Barcola, Alexis Mac Allister would not have such worries just minutes later.

The midfielder, who recently confirmed Liverpool did not intend to offer him a new contract, let rip with a thunderous left-footed strike from just outside the box to put the hosts in the lead.

4 Llorente has proved to be a constant thorn in Liverpool's side Credit: Getty

4

4 But Mac Allister ensured it would be a winning start in Europe for Liverpool Credit: Getty

Marcos Llorente opened the scoring in the 17th minute when he ghosted past Milos Kerkez and fizzed a driven effort past Alisson.

It was the tenth goal of Llorente's career in the competition.

Remarkably, five of those have been scored against Liverpool, all of which have come at Anfield.

It took Liverpool until the 40th minute to equalise, with Dominik Szoboszlai the man to bring the scores level.

However, most of the plaudits for the equaliser went to Ronald Araujo as he nutmegged an Atleti defender with a deft flick that went straight to Szoboszlai, who then stroked the ball past Jan Oblak.

Frimpong then thought he doubled Liverpool's advantage just before second-half stoppage time when he scored on the rebound from close range.

However, it was immediately ruled out for offside, with replays confirming the on-field decision.

Liverpool's next outing sees them entertain Fulham on Saturday with their next Champions League game away at Austrian side LASK on October 14.

Sports.title: Adel Taarabt blew Man United move after fight with teammate, rejected Arsenal and went out the night before games
Sports.content:
Adel Taarabt blew Man United move after fight with teammate, rejected Arsenal and went out the night before games

Adel Taarabt became a cult hero at QPR, and it’s fair to say his antics might not have been tolerated anywhere else.

After calling time on a memorable career which saw him dazzle Premier League fans with his skill and flair, the Moroccan joined talkSPORT Drive to reveal all about his days in the limelight.



6 Taarabt showcased his immense talent at QPR Credit: Getty

The streets won't forget

Taarabt's name is one remembered fondly by English football supporters, especially at QPR.

While his playing days saw him turn out for the likes of Tottenham, AC Milan and Benfica, he is best known for his time at Loftus Road.

A mercurial talent, Taarabt first joined the Hoops on loan from Spurs in 2009 before signing permanently, and went on to make 164 appearances, scoring 34 goals and assisting 41 more.



During this time he became a cult icon, as his outrageous skills and dribbling ability saw him deliver arguably the the best individual season in Championship history in the 2010/11 season.

He scored 19 goals and provided 16 assists to guide QPR back to the Premier League, before going on to dazzle in the top flight.



Taarabt reveals Sir Alex Ferguson U-turn

Taarabt's stunning displays at QPR made him one of football's most exciting prospects and he was often heavily tipped for a big move.

Among his admirers were a dominant Manchester United managed by the legendary Sir Alex Ferguson, who even travelled to Hull to catch him in action in a Championship clash in January 2011.



But Taarabt has revealed any chance of a move fell apart after chaos ensued when he fought with senior teammate Shaun Derry.

He told talkSPORT Drive: “There was one time, we were first in the Championship and I know that game, Sir Alex Ferguson came only for me.

“We were playing at Hull City, and he just came because he wanted to sign me.

6 Known for his tough love approach, Fergie didn't fancy taking on Taarabt's strong character Credit: Getty



“Then after 42 minutes, I fought with Shan Derry during the game and I went to the touchline. I said to [my manager] Neil Warnock, ‘You’re gonna change me now, I'm going out.’

“And then Ferguson said, ‘What? He's crazy this boy'."

While Ferguson had seen enough, such was Taarabt's importance at QPR that his manager - the iconic Neil Warnock - ignored his calls to be substituted and instead took aim at Derry.

He continued: “Neil Warnock said, ‘No, I'm not going change you, stay here’. I was just standing for four minutes on the touchline. I said ‘Change me. I want to go out.’

“And then after half time, Neil Warnock went and destroyed Shaun Derry.



“He said, ‘This is the first and last time you speak to him. If he wants the ball, give him it. Don't talk to him, otherwise I’ll change you, you will never play for me’.

6 While a big move never materialised, Taarabt instead became a Premier League fan favourite with QPR Credit: Getty

“And then after that, I think Sir Alex Ferguson said: 'I cannot take a boy with this mentality'.”

Turning down Arsenal

While Taarabt saw any chance of a move to Man United disappear in a flash, he turned down a chance to join Arsenal on his own terms.



Despite being offered opportunity to play European football under another icon in Arsene Wenger, the maverick star revealed he opted to stay at QPR as he was earning better wages, and was keen to avoid a repeat of his struggles at Spurs.

He explained: “I spoke with Wenger and he told me to come, he said, ‘I will offer you with Champions League [football]'.

“But already, what he offered me on wages was much lower than what I was earning at QPR before I signed my new contract.

“In the end I said: ‘No, if QPR is going to give me a new contract, I'm not coming to Arsenal and having to fight for your position, [where you’re] not sure if you’ll play every week.



6 Arsene Wenger's legendary coaching career was not enough to convince Taarabt to join Arsenal Credit: AFP

“So even though it was a good offer, I said, ‘No, I'm not going.”

London's night owl

While most players would feel the pressure to perform as their team's star player, Taarabt was the opposite.

The Hoops legend admitted he'd often be out until the early hours the night before a game, with his love of London's nightlife such that Drive host and former Spurs teammate Darren Bent once claiming this prompted Taarabt to turn down a move to Liverpool.

Taarabt admitted: “Sometimes the day of the game I was going out."

He added: “Let's say Saturday, I'd go out on Friday night and then we’d have meeting at Loftus Road at one o'clock for the game at three."



Most managers might take a dim view to this approach - especially from their captain - but not the legendary Warnock.

6 Under Warnock's management, Taarabt helped end QPR's 15-year absence from the Premier League with promotion in 2011 Credit: Getty

Explaining how he juggled his social life and QPR responsibilities, Taarabt brazenly said: "At that age, for me it was really easy.

“I was the captain so before the match we’d go to see the referee with the coach - so with Neil.



“He told me: ‘Listen, son I know you were out last night, but just go out there and win the game for me’.”

Taarabt and Neil Warnock

Taarabt's unique relationship with then QPR boss Warnock is no secret, with the popular English manager previously revealing he bent his own rules to accommodate the player's strong personality given his huge talent.

But asked about Warnock's role in his career, Taarabt cheekily quipped: “I think I was more important to him than he was to me!”

Opening up on the special treatment he received at QPR, he then shared: "Sometimes I wasn't training five days [a week]. I'd just come on Friday, and play Saturdays!"



Taarabt added: "Neil Warnock - he's not crazy tactically or sometimes his training, I didn't like.

“So he just told me: ‘You just have to come [when you want] to be happy’.”

6 Juande Ramos guided Spurs to League Cup glory in 2008, but Taarabt did not enjoy his time under the Spaniard Credit: Getty

Juande Ramos labelled the 'worst'

With Warnock clearly a favourite manager in his career, Taarabt was less glowing about one coach during his time at Tottenham.



After joining the club under Martin Jol in 2007, the enigmatic former star struggled for game time - making just 15 appearances overall - and things went from bad to worse when Juande Ramos took over.

Discussing his first pre-season at Spurs, Taarabt told talkSPORT: “I was thinking I'm gonna start the season on fire.

“Then suddenly I was dropped, not playing. But it was not a stable club - every six months [they were] changing coach and for a young player it's not good.

“The worst one was Ramos - I could not understand anything from this guy. After that I said: ‘[It’s] better I leave’.”

Sports.title: Chelsea vs Leeds kick-off delayed just 20 minutes before game was due to start
Sports.content:
Chelsea vs Leeds kick-off delayed just 20 minutes before game was due to start

Chelsea's barnstorming Carabao Cup tie against Leeds United was delayed.

The Blues confirmed in a statement that kick-off at Stamford Bridge had been pushed back by 15 minutes.



4 The Blues players' preparation took a slight hit Credit: Getty

As a result, the match started at 8:15pm, rather than 8pm.

Why was Chelsea's Carabao Cup game against Leeds delayed?

According to a screen within Stamford Bridge, the reason behind the delay was due to 'an issue with the rail network'.

The Transport for London site states that there are 'severe delays' on the District, Circle and Hammersmith and City lines.

Emergency services were dispatched earlier on Wednesday to deal with a casualty on the track.



The transport issues impacted the kick-off time because the nearest tube station to Stamford Bridge, Fulham Broadway, is situated on the District line.

How did the match between Chelsea and Leeds unfold?

It was worth the wait for the spectators, who were treated to a nine-goal thriller with Chelsea prevailing 6-3 on Wednesday.



The visitors struck first courtesy of Tarik Muharemovic before Brenden Aaronson doubled their advantage just after the half time break.

But Chelsea then turned on the style, with Cole Palmer netting twice in the space of two minutes.



Pedro Neto bagged Chelsea's third on the hour mark before summer signing Danny Welbeck made it four shortly after.

Leeds were understandably shell-shocked having coughed up four goals in the space of 12 minutes, but Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave them a sniff of hope when he scored in the 75th minute.

4 Palmer began the Chelsea fightback, scoring two of their six goals Credit: Getty

4 Welbeck now has three goals for the Blues since he joined Credit: Getty



However, a goal from Valentin Barco and a stoppage-time header from Welbeck put the result beyond doubt as Chelsea progressed to the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

How did Chelsea and Leeds line up for the Carabao Cup third round match?

Blues boss Xabi Alonso elected to give several of his key players a rest in Wednesday's encounter as he made a whopping nine changes to the line-up that fell 2-1 to Arsenal on Sunday.

Mike Penders, Levi Colwill, Malo Gusto, Pep Chavarria, Barco, Estevao, Jamie Gittens and Welbeck all came into the starting 11.

Alonso also boldly handed a debut to 16-year-old midfielder Reggie Watson.



Like Chelsea, Leeds made a significant amount of changes - eight to be exact - to the starting line-up.

In the new-look side, Leeds boss Daniel Farke handed debuts to goalkeeper Michael Zetterer and defender Melvin Bard.

4 Despite the mass changes, Chelsea avoided a surprise loss Credit: Getty

Zetterer joined from Eintracht Frankfurt while Bard moved from Nice on a season-long loan.



What is the recent record between Chelsea and Leeds?

Chelsea went into Wednesday's clash hoping to make it three games unbeaten against Leeds.

The Blues prevailed 1-0 in their last encounter, which was a FA Cup semi-final tie in April.

Prior to that, the two sides played out a 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge in February.

Leeds' last win away at Stamford Bridge came in December 1999, when they prevailed 2-0.

Sports.title: ‘Get a life’ – Non-league club report individual for impersonating manager and giving bogus offers
Sports.content:
Non league club Gainsborough Trinity is 'aware' of an individual is impersonating their manager Russ Wilcox.

The individual, while posing as Wilcox, has proposed wage offers and potential transfers to players.



2 Someone is pretending to be Wilcox (left) Credit: Getty

The Northern Premier League, the seventh tier of English football, and the Football Association have both been made aware of the incidents.

FA regulations prohibit direct contact between managers and players, with all transfer approaches required to go through formal club-to-club communications.

Gainsborough Trinity CEO issues statement

"We want to make it categorically clear that these approaches have not been made by Russ Wilcox, nor have they been made on behalf of Gainsborough Trinity Football Club," Gainsborough chief executive Matt Boles said in a statement.



"We strongly condemn the actions of the individual responsible. Impersonating a football manager and making false representations to players is completely unacceptable and has the potential to cause unnecessary disruption and reputational damage to players, managers and clubs."

Boles also expressed gratitude to managers and club officials who reached out directly to Wilcox after they received an approach from the individual who impersonated the coach.



"Finally, to the person responsible: enough is enough," Boles continued.

"Stop impersonating our manager, stop wasting the time of players and clubs across the non-league game and, quite frankly, get a life."



Russ Wilcox's coaching career at a glance

Wilcox has been in charge of Lincolnshire-based Gainsborough since September 2023.

He has previously managed Scunthorpe United, York City and Farsley Celtic over the course of a decade.

Prior to his managerial career, Wilcox spent time working as an assistant coach under Brian Laws.

Wilcox followed Laws from Scunthorpe to Sheffield Wednesday in 2006.

2 Gainsborough reached the first round proper of last season's FA Cup Credit: Getty



The pair reunited at Burnley in January 2010, but could not save the club from Premier League relegation at the end of the 2009/10 campaign.

How have Gainsborough Trinity performed this season?

Gainsborough play in the seventh tier of English football and are currently eighth in the league table, one place outside the Northern Premier League's Premier Division play-off spots this term.

Wilcox's side have won four, drawn once and lost three times in their first eight league fixtures to sit on 13 points, six behind league leaders Cleethorpes Town.

Gainsborough will look to put the off-field drama behind them when they host Avro on Saturday.



The club then travels to Leamington on September 19 in FA Cup second qualifying round.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers jokingly brands Cole Palmer winning player of the match 'criminal' in video after Chelsea's madcap 6-3 win over Leeds
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers jokingly labelled Cole Palmer's player of the match award as 'criminal' after being overlooked following his performance in their 6-3 win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup. Chelsea had looked at risk of crashing out at the third round stage after trailing 2-0 at Stamford Bridge. The introduction of Rogers and Palmer among four half-time substitutes had helped the Blues to fight back in the second half. Palmer scored twice in three minutes, including scoring from the penalty spot, to bring Chelsea back level. His second was one of three assists from Rogers, with the £117million summer signing also laying on goals for Pedro Neto and Danny Welbeck as Chelsea took charge. Valentin Barco and a late second from Welbeck, either side of Dominic Calvert-Lewin netting for Leeds – ultimately helped Chelsea seal a 6-3 win to progress. "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk — Sky Sports Football (@SkyFootball) September 9, 2026 Morgan Rogers joked Cole Palmer receiving the player of the match award was 'criminal' after Chelsea's 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds Palmer scored twice as Chelsea came from 2-0 down while Rogers provided three assists Palmer noted that his penalty sparked Chelsea's comeback as the pair joked post-match Rogers, who believed he had four assists, had jokingly expressed frustration in a post-match interview after discovering Palmer had landed the player of the match award over him. 'Mate, I got four assists,' Rogers said. 'I can't believe that, that is mental, he scored a pen.' Palmer responded: 'I started the comeback, I will shout you out, I'll shout you out and say you should have had it.' Rogers continued with his mock outrage, adding: 'That is mental, don't mention me, I am just a bystander, that is criminal.' When he was asked whether he would present the trophy to Palmer, Rogers quipped: 'I will unfortunately yes, it is rigged.' Rogers, who had previously played with his close friend Palmer as a youngster at Man City, did underline his excitement at playing for Chelsea after their impressive start to the season. 'The environment, the players, the coaching staff have allowed me in and let me show what I'm about,' Rogers said. 'To play with this calibre of players makes my life a lot easier. I can show my ability to the best of what's possible, and it's a really enjoyable team to play in. 'You can see it [building something special]. There's a lot to work on and it's early days but seeing these signs so early, it doesn't normally happen quite this early. 'It's exciting but we've still got a long way to go and a lot to achieve.'

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard is on a mission to put himself at top table of elite midfielders as captain's brilliance gives Arsenal the perfect start to Champions League campaign with victory at Napoli
Sports.content:
Arsenal issued a warning to their own fans before kick-off in Naples, strongly advising them not to wear club shirts or scarves, or use public transport to avoid being targeted by Napoli ultras. That was their biggest statement of the day — before Martin Odegaard, whose previous season was tarnished by injury and loss of form, ensured those travelling fans would be heading home in high spirits. As Christos Tzolis’s pass reached the Norwegian just outside the area, his eyes lit up, driving forward on that wand of a left foot. Once he saw a gap, the captain curled the ball with pace and precision into the bottom left-corner to get Arsenal’s Champions League campaign off to a winning start. It’s now four goals in five matches for Odegaard, who has entered this season on a mission to prove himself at the top table of elite midfielders after just one goal across all competitions last term. Runners up in both 2006 and 2026 — either side of a crushing Europa League final loss to Chelsea under Unai Emery — the Champions League remains Arsenal’s last frontier. A September night in Naples doesn’t dictate where the trophy will lie, but builds momentum and helps bypass the dreaded play-off round. They ought to use this result as a lesson going forward. Martin Odegaard score the only goal as last year's runners-up Arsenal began their Champions League campaign with a 1-0 win over Napoli Odegaard scored a stunning effort from outside the area to break the deadlock in Naples Mikel Arteta's side dominated the game but were made to wait for their opening goal Bukayo Saka blazed over from close range in Arsenal's best chance of the first half ‘That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game,’ manager Mikel Arteta said of Odegaard. ‘I feel he has this emotional state that he knows that the ball can go in and he is playing an incredible football match.’ By the 50-minute mark, Arsenal had Napoli camped around their own box, hoping for the pressure to relent. They struggled to get out and, on the rare occasion Napoli did, their attacks were snuffed out. Luckily for them, the Gunners didn’t come bearing a full arsenal — until Odegaard’s intervention. Viktor Gyokeres was given a rare start in place of Kai Havertz, using his physicality to hold up the ball. There was the odd moment of brilliance, such as an instep cross which Bukayo Saka tried meeting with a scissor-kick. MATCH FACTS AND RATINGS NAPOLI (4-3-3): Meret 6.5 (Milinkovic-Savic 46mins, 6.5); Di Lorenzo 6.5, Rrahmani 6.5, Marin 6.5, Olivera 6.5; Gilmour 6, Lobotka 6, De Bruyne 6.5; Politano 6 (Favasuli 58, 6), Hojlund 5, Alisson Santos 5 (Vergara 58, 6). Manager: Massimiliano Allegri 6. ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; White 6.5, Konsa 6.5, Gabriel 6.5, Hincapie 6; Rice 7.5, Merino 6.5 (Guimaraes 66, 6); Saka 6, Odegaard 8, Eze 6 (Tzolis 66, 6.5); Gyokeres 5.5. Goals: Odegaard Manager: Mikel Arteta 6.5. Referee: Glenn Nyberg 6.5. However, a theme of wastefulness ran through Arteta’s side. Chance after chance arrived, the ball either ending up in half-time substitute goalkeeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic’s grasp or well beyond the goal frame. Arteta at least showed he’d learned from the previous campaign, making four changes to the side which beat Chelsea on Sunday — Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Gyokeres making their first starts of the season. Saka’s looping cross to the back post reached Eze, who nodded the ball to Merino but his resulting header, with plenty of neck swivel, was palmed over by Alex Meret. Before the first half ended, Odegaard played Saka through, the winger hoofing the ball when one-v-one with the keeper. It was ruled offside, to spare his blushes. The triumvirate of Saka, Odegaard and Ben White were in sync, quick passes constantly exchanged to caused the hosts’ backline many a problem and give Saka avenues to get forward. Hincapie ought to have scored five minutes after the break. Odegaard’s clever, looping chip found White, his header teeing up Hincapie’s wild blaze over the bar. Arteta turned to Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes and Havertz later and that soon helped change the game.
