World.title: CBN warns banks, fintechs over cyber risks
World.content:
…Says weak links could destabilise financial system

By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

ABUJA: The Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, has urged banks, fintechs and other financial institutions to treat cybersecurity and third-party technology risks as critical financial stability issues, warning that vulnerabilities in one institution could trigger widespread disruption across the financial system.

The Director, Payments System Supervision at the CBN and Chairperson of the Nigeria Electronic Fraud Forum, NeFF, Dr Rakiya Yusuf, gave the warning at the 19th Annual Banking and Finance Conference of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria, CIBN, in Abuja.

Speaking during a session titled, “Navigating Cyber and Systemic Risks in the AI-Driven Future of Banking: Implications for Financial Stability and Business Resilience,” Yusuf said the growing reliance of financial institutions on fintechs, payment service providers, cloud operators and other technology vendors had created new channels for cyber and systemic risks.

She warned that a weakness in a bank, fintech, payment service provider or technology vendor could spread rapidly across interconnected institutions, creating what she described as a “one-fire” effect capable of destabilising the entire financial system.

Yusuf said financial institutions must therefore move beyond securing their internal systems to strengthening safeguards across the wider financial ecosystem.

She urged banks and other operators to continuously assess their dependencies, third-party relationships and technology partners to determine how disruptions in one part of the ecosystem could affect their operations.

The CBN director stressed that operational resilience involved more than preventing cyberattacks, noting that institutions must also be able to maintain critical services during disruptions and recover quickly from incidents.

She disclosed that the CBN was strengthening its regulatory framework, supervisory processes and policy measures to identify and address vulnerabilities capable of threatening financial stability before they materialise.

According to her, cyber and operational risk considerations were now being integrated into the product approval process to ensure that new financial products did not introduce systemic vulnerabilities.

Yusuf also urged financial institutions to extend cybersecurity and risk-management oversight to third-party service providers.

She said banks must assess the capacity of their technology partners to withstand and recover from cyberattacks and major operational failures.

The CBN director called for prompt reporting of cyber incidents and vulnerabilities to regulators, saying early disclosure would enable timely intervention before isolated breaches escalated into systemic threats.

She also advocated greater intelligence and information sharing among financial institutions, noting that stronger collaboration would improve the industry’s ability to detect emerging threats and coordinate responses.

Yusuf recommended the establishment of stronger Security Operations Centres, SOCs, capable of monitoring cyber threats across the financial ecosystem in real time.

On the growing adoption of artificial intelligence, she cautioned that innovation must be matched with accountability, insisting that automation should not eliminate human responsibility from financial decisions.

She described the approach as “automating accountability,” explaining that while AI could perform increasingly sophisticated tasks, human oversight must remain central to decisions affecting customers and the financial system.

Yusuf further urged financial institutions to strengthen data governance and pay greater attention to digital sovereignty by examining where critical data were stored, who had access to them, what intelligence could be derived from them and how such data influenced decision-making.

She warned that placing critical data or key technological capabilities beyond an institution’s effective control could expose the financial system to additional risks.

Yusuf maintained that safeguarding Nigeria’s financial system required a collective approach involving regulators, banks, fintechs, payment service providers and technology companies.

She said the objective should be to build a resilient ecosystem capable of absorbing shocks, containing cyber incidents and recovering swiftly without allowing the failure of one institution to threaten the stability of the entire financial system.

World.title: Diphtheria: No outbreak in Lagos – Abayomi
World.content:
… Says 53 suspected cases recorded this year

… Urges parents to complete children’s 3 immunization doses

By Chioma Obinna

The Lagos state Commissioner for Health, Prof Akin Abayomi on Wednesday raised its disease surveillance and preparedness against diphtheria, warning residents not to panic but to remain vigilant as the outbreak continues to spread in parts of Nigeria.

Abayomi, however, said there is currently no outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos, despite recording 53 suspected cases in 2026, six of which were laboratory-confirmed.

The Commissioner, who gave the assurance at a media briefing on the state’s diphtheria preparedness and response, said the government was taking precautionary measures because of the high level of movement between Lagos and states currently battling the disease.

According to him, the situation requires vigilance because Lagos’ huge population and extensive connections with other parts of the country could facilitate community transmission if imported cases are not detected and managed early.

“We are appealing to all Lagosians to remain calm. There is no current outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos. We are simply taking precautionary measures,” Abayomi said.

The Commissioner said the government was particularly concerned about the outbreak reported in states including Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Benue and Zamfara, noting that the continuous movement of people between Lagos and affected areas made surveillance imperative.

“We are watching this outbreak expand, and we are cautious in Lagos, as always. The Executive Council always likes to err on the side of caution and increase our prevention strategies in the state,” he said.

Abayomi explained that diphtheria is a serious bacterial respiratory infection capable of causing life-threatening complications when treatment is delayed.

He said the disease could produce a toxin capable of attacking the heart, while swelling and a thick membrane in the throat could obstruct breathing and swallowing.

“There are two major things that happen to a patient with diphtheria. First, it can block the breathing apparatus in the throat, preventing the person from breathing normally or swallowing liquids and food properly.

“Secondly, the toxin can enter the blood and travel to the heart, causing problems with the heartbeat and, eventually, heart failure.”

He warned that an undiagnosed infection could therefore progress rapidly into airway obstruction and inflammation of the heart.

Abayomi urged anyone developing severe sore throat, fever, weakness, neck swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing, particularly after travelling to an affected state or having contact with a confirmed case, to seek medical attention immediately.

“If you have any of these symptoms, present yourself quickly to one of our primary healthcare centres or your doctor so that we can make the diagnosis, carry out the necessary diagnostic workup and start treatment as quickly as possible,” he said.

Giving an update on the situation in Lagos, Abayomi disclosed that 53 suspected diphtheria cases had been recorded in the state so far in 2026.

Only six, he said, were confirmed through laboratory diagnosis, with all six cases appropriately managed.

He added that contacts of confirmed patients were traced and placed under observation throughout the incubation period to detect possible secondary infections.

“In Lagos, we have had sporadic cases of diphtheria. In fact, in 2026, we have had 53 suspected cases. Of those 53, only six have been confirmed through laboratory diagnosis,” he said.

The Commissioner stressed that early diagnosis significantly improves the chances of successful treatment.

“The treatment for diphtheria is very effective if the disease is diagnosed early,” Abayomi said, explaining that treatment involves antibiotics and medication capable of neutralising the toxin produced by the bacteria.

While stressing that immunisation remains the most effective protection against diphtheria, Abayomi disclosed that only about 64 per cent of children in Lagos have received full vaccination coverage.

He urged parents and guardians to check their children’s immunisation records and ensure that they receive all three doses of the pentavalent vaccine.

“If you have received three doses, then you have significant protection. If you have received two, one or none, then you are vulnerable,” he warned.

According to him, the three doses are expected to be administered at six, 10 and 14 weeks.

He said Lagos has more than 1,000 healthcare facilities providing routine immunisation services across the public and private sectors, with vaccines available free at government facilities.

The Commissioner clarified that primary healthcare centres are mainly vaccination points and are not the facilities designated to diagnose and manage suspected diphtheria cases.

He listed the four designated centres as the Infectious Disease Hospital, Yaba; Massey Street Children’s Hospital, Lagos Island; Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH; and Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH.

“If we suspect a case of diphtheria, we refer the patient to designated facilities. These are the four centres where we actively manage suspected cases of diphtheria. They have the capacity to make the diagnosis and manage the complications,” Abayomi said.

He noted that severe cases could require advanced intervention to maintain the patient’s airway and close monitoring of the heart to prevent fatal complications.

With schools expected to reopen soon, Abayomi said the Ministry of Health was working with the education sector to strengthen awareness and vaccination among schoolchildren.

He said suspected cases in schools would trigger contact tracing and other infection-control measures.

The Commissioner also urged residents to observe basic respiratory hygiene, including covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, washing hands regularly and avoiding close contact with others when experiencing respiratory symptoms.

Speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr. Dayo Lajide, also appealed to parents to ensure their children are fully vaccinated.

“More importantly, we have to make sure that all our children are vaccinated,” Lajide said.

She also urged the media to play a responsible role by providing accurate information to prevent unnecessary panic while encouraging residents to take appropriate preventive measures.

She added that the government’s heightened surveillance was not a declaration of an outbreak in Lagos, but a precautionary response designed to ensure that any suspected case is detected, isolated, investigated and treated before it can trigger wider transmission.

World.title: Yobe LG poll: ADC alleges exclusion by YSIEC
World.content:
By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu

DAMATURU — The Yobe State chapter of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, has accused the Yobe State Independent Electoral Commission, YSIEC, of excluding the party from crucial electoral information ahead of the 2026 local government election.

The party threatened to seek legal redress and organise peaceful protests if the commission fails to address its concerns.

ADC made the allegations in a letter of concern addressed to the Chairman of YSIEC, expressing what it described as “serious concern and disappointment” over the commission’s alleged failure to communicate election guidelines, timetable and other electoral decisions affecting its participation.

The party said equal and meaningful access to electoral information was essential to the lawful participation of political parties in an election.

It therefore demanded evidence of when, how and through which official channel the relevant guidelines, timetable and electoral decisions were communicated to it.

“We therefore request clear evidence of when, how and through what official channel the relevant Guidelines, timetable and electoral decisions were communicated to ADC,” the party stated.

According to ADC, failure to properly notify it of electoral requirements could prejudice its ability to participate fully in the council election.

The party cited Sections 7, 40 and 197 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Third Schedule, applicable electoral laws and YSIEC regulations in support of its concerns.

ADC warned that it would pursue all lawful avenues if any action or omission by the commission affected its participation in the electoral process.

“ADC hereby puts YSIEC on notice that, if our lawful rights or participation have been prejudiced by any failure of notification, we will pursue every lawful avenue available to protect our rights,” it stated.

The party said such measures could include legal action, media engagement, social media advocacy and peaceful public protest.

ADC also called on the commission to provide clarification and take appropriate corrective action if its participation had been affected by any failure of notification.

The letter, dated September 2026, was addressed to the YSIEC Chairman, with copies sent to the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, the Yobe State Government, the Political Adviser to the Governor, the Commissioner of Police, the state command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and the Department of State Services.

As of the time of filing this report, YSIEC had not publicly responded to the allegations contained in the ADC letter.

The development comes as political parties prepare for the 2026 local government election in the state.

World.title: Tinubu’s wife empowers 500 women in Ebonyi
World.content:
First Lady Oluremi Tinubu

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

ABAKALIKI — Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has distributed empowerment items to 500 indigent women in Ebonyi State to support them in starting new businesses or improving existing enterprises.

The items included deep freezers, gas cookers with ovens, power generators and industrial grinding machines.

Tinubu, who was represented by the wife of the Ebonyi State Governor, Mrs Mary-Maudline Uzoamaka Nwifuru, said the empowerment programme was being implemented simultaneously in the five states of the South-East.

She said the initiative was made possible through the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs.

According to her, the programme was designed to empower 18,000 women nationwide, with 500 beneficiaries selected from each state and the Federal Capital Territory.

She said: “This presentation is taking place across the five states of the zone simultaneously.

“This programme has been made possible through the Office of the SSA to the President on Sustainable Development Goals.

“The initiative was first launched in Abuja for the North-Central zone in February 2025, followed by the distribution of empowerment items in the South-South zone on April 25, 2026, and the South-West zone on August 23, 2025.

“By the end of the nationwide rollout of this initiative, 18,000 women would have been empowered across the country, with 500 beneficiaries selected from each state and the FCT.”

She said the programme aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Initiative, particularly in recognising the critical role women play in nation-building.

She urged the beneficiaries to use the items judiciously to achieve the objectives of the programme.

The representative of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on SDGs, Dr Ify Ukaegbu, also urged the beneficiaries not to sell the items.

Ukaegbu said the intervention was aimed at expanding economic opportunities for indigent and vulnerable women across the country.

Some of the beneficiaries expressed appreciation to the President’s wife and the wife of the Ebonyi State Governor for the gesture, saying the items would enable them to become self-reliant and support their families.

They pledged to use the items judiciously, adding that the intervention came at a time when they needed support to establish sustainable means of livelihood.

World.title: Unilorin don urges FG to prioritise aquaculture
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi

ILORIN: A Professor of Agriculture and Fisheries at the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, Wasiu Adeyemi Jimoh, has urged the Federal Government to make sustainable aquaculture a strategic component of Nigeria’s food security, nutrition and economic development agenda.

Jimoh said increased investment in aquaculture could accelerate the development of a resilient, environmentally sustainable and globally competitive industry capable of creating jobs, reducing dependence on fish imports and contributing significantly to national economic growth.

He made the call while delivering the 306th inaugural lecture of the University of Ilorin, titled, “Green Feeds, Healthy Fish: Enhancing Aquaculture Productivity,” at the university auditorium on Monday.

The don said the sector could be strengthened through increased investment in research, innovation, human capacity development and the commercialisation of locally developed technologies.

According to him, “Investment in aquaculture will accelerate the transition towards a resilient, environmentally sustainable, and globally competitive industry, capable of creating employment, reducing import dependence, and contributing significantly to national economic development.”

He added that strategic implementation of the proposed measures would transform aquaculture into a resilient, environmentally restorative and economically viable sector.

Jimoh said the development of the sector was essential to achieving food and nutrition security, creating sustainable employment and improving livelihoods for present and future generations.

He explained that his research had focused on developing alternatives to conventional fish feed ingredients through the use of plant-based protein sources, phytogenic additives and circular-economy principles.

“These efforts aimed to reduce dependence on fishmeal and soybean meal, optimise nutrient utilisation, enhance fish health, and improve economic sustainability for fish farmers,” he said.

The professor noted that fish remained one of the most nutrient-dense and accessible sources of protein, providing high-quality amino acids, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins and minerals.

He said fish was particularly important in developing countries where malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies remained challenges, adding that it served as both a source of nutrition and livelihood for millions of people.

Jimoh also called on feed manufacturers, veterinary professionals, fish health specialists and regulatory agencies to formulate, certify and promote functional aquafeeds for fish farmers.

He advocated the routine use of aquafeeds containing probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics and natural immunostimulants, saying they could strengthen disease prevention, reduce antibiotic misuse and improve fish welfare and productivity.

“Fish occupy a unique and irreplaceable position in the global landscape, influencing dietary patterns, shaping economic activities, and fostering traditions that are deeply rooted in historical and ecological contexts.

“Fish are not merely food sources but a lifeline that sustains billions of people worldwide. From the bustling fish markets of Asia to the artisanal fisheries of Africa, fish form the bedrock of diets, livelihoods, and communities,” he said.

World.title: Gombe JPDA DG highlights three years of projects
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

GOMBE — The Director-General of the Gombe State Joint Projects Development and Essential Social Services Agency, JPDA, Dr Mahmood Yusuf, has highlighted the agency’s projects across the state in his three years in office, describing the period as one of institutional growth, leadership experience and grassroots development.

Yusuf, a Fellow of the Nigerian Institute of Building, FNIOB, also expressed appreciation to Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for the opportunity to serve in the position.

The agency, formerly known as the Gombe State Joint Projects Development Agency, has expanded its mandate to include essential social services and developmental interventions across the state.

Reflecting on his stewardship, Yusuf said his three years in office had provided valuable lessons in leadership, public service, accountability and human relations.

“Working directly under His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has made me understand that leadership is ultimately about the impact one makes in the lives of others,” he said.

He said the experience had broadened his understanding of public service, particularly the importance of prudence, effective communication and listening to diverse opinions.

According to Yusuf, the agency has executed projects across the state’s 11 local government areas, covering infrastructure, grassroots administration, markets, traditional institutions, security facilities and renewable energy.

In Akko Local Government Area, he listed the reconstruction of the local government secretariat and Gona Emir’s Palace, installation of solar streetlights in Kumo and Tumfure, and construction of the Akko West LCDA Secretariat in Pindiga and Akko North LCDA Secretariat in Amada.

In Balanga, the agency provided a one-megawatt solar mini-grid for Tallasse and Swa communities and constructed the Balanga South LCDA Secretariat in Bambam.

Billiri benefited from the reconstruction of the Gada-Uku-Sansani Bridge, construction of a police outpost at Amtawalam, reconstruction of Kantoma Market, construction of the Billiri Grains Market and the Billiri West LCDA Secretariat at Tal.

In Dukku, projects included a motor park, grains and cattle market, solar streetlights and the Dukku North LCDA Secretariat at Malala.

Yusuf said Funakaye received the reconstruction of the Emir’s Palace and 12 district head palaces, construction of 66 shops in Bajoga, solar streetlights in Bajoga and Ashaka, and the Funakaye South LCDA Secretariat in Tongo.

In Gombe Local Government Area, the agency reconstructed the Idi Shopping Complex and Gombe Emir’s Palace, as well as constructed the Gombe South LCDA Secretariat in Bolari.

Projects in Kwami included the reconstruction and furnishing of 11 district head palaces, solar streetlights in several communities and the Kwami West LCDA Secretariat in Bojude.

In Kaltungo, the agency reconstructed the local government secretariat, constructed market stalls and built the Kaltungo East LCDA Secretariat at Tula Wange.

Nafada Local Government Area benefited from the construction of its local government secretariat, solar streetlights in Nafada and surrounding communities, and the Nafada South LCDA Secretariat at Birin Fulani.

In Shongom, projects included part of the local government secretariat, seven district head palaces, a 650KWH solar mini-grid in Filiya and the Pero-Chonge LCDA Secretariat.

In Yamaltu/Deba, the agency provided fencing, solar streetlights and a solar-powered borehole with four fetching points at the National Agricultural Land Development Authority, NALDA, Market in Kwadon.

Solar streetlights were also installed in Deba, Dadin Kowa, Hinna, Kwadon, Wajari, Gwani, Shinga and Wade, while the Yamaltu East and Yamaltu West LCDA secretariats were constructed at Dadin Kowa and Zambuk respectively.

Yusuf further disclosed that the construction of the Gombe State Council of Emirs and Chiefs Secretariat had reached about 95 per cent completion.

He said the project, when completed, would provide a befitting institutional structure for traditional leadership in the state.

The JPDA boss attributed the achievements to the support and guidance of Governor Inuwa Yahaya, as well as the cooperation of stakeholders, staff and communities.

He expressed optimism that the agency would continue to contribute to the implementation of projects aimed at improving the living conditions of residents.

“I sincerely thank everyone for their unwavering support throughout this journey. The achievements recorded are a product of collective effort, and I hope we will continue to work together to move our dear state forward,” Yusuf said.

World.title: Gombe women mobilise over 6,000 for unity summit
World.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

GOMBE — More than 6,000 women from across Gombe State on Wednesday converged on the APC Square, Gombe, for the maiden Gombe Women’s Unity and Progress Summit convened by Dr Zainab Jamil Gwamna.

The summit, held under the theme, “Stronger Voices, United Women, Greater Impact,” brought together women from the state’s 11 local government areas and 13 Local Council Development Areas, including entrepreneurs, professionals, community leaders, political stakeholders and women advocates.

According to a statement by Ibrahim Sani Shawai, spokesperson to the APC governorship candidate in Gombe State, Dr Jamil Isyaku Gwamna, the summit was designed to promote unity, empowerment, mentorship and greater participation of women in governance and socio-economic development.

Speaking at the event, the convener, Dr Zainab Gwamna, said the initiative was aimed at building a united women’s movement capable of supporting one another and creating opportunities for younger generations.

“This summit is about bringing Gombe women together to discover our collective strength and understand that the success of one woman should open doors for another,” she said.

“We must mentor our young girls, support women in business and professions, strengthen our families and contribute meaningfully to our communities.”

Gwamna commended the turnout, describing it as an indication of the potential of women to contribute to social and economic development.

She also commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for programmes targeted at women and youths, while appreciating her husband, Dr Jamil Gwamna, for his support.

The convener urged participants to take the lessons and relationships developed at the summit back to their communities, with emphasis on mentoring young girls, skills acquisition, confidence building and economic self-reliance.

Also speaking, the wife of the Gombe State Governor, Dr Asma’u Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, commended the initiative and the turnout of women from across the state.

She reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to programmes aimed at improving the welfare, empowerment and economic wellbeing of women and youths.

“Women are indispensable partners in the development of our families, communities and the state,” she said.

“I commend Dr Zainab Gwamna for bringing women together through this important summit and for creating a platform where they can learn, connect and support one another.”

Dr Asma’u encouraged the participants to sustain the spirit of unity, cooperation and mutual support demonstrated at the gathering.

Participants from different professional and community backgrounds also commended the initiative, saying sustained collaboration, mentorship and economic empowerment were important to increasing women’s participation in development.

Some participants expressed optimism that the networks established at the summit would continue beyond the event and create opportunities for women and young girls across the state.

The gathering also had political undertones, with some political stakeholders saying the mobilisation could strengthen the grassroots support base of the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

However, the central message of the summit was the need for women to support one another, mentor younger generations and use collective action to promote social and economic development in Gombe State.

World.title: Polaris Bank manager killed in Imo kidnapping attack
World.content:
OWERRI — Polaris Bank has expressed grief over the killing of one of its branch managers, identified as Mr Ossy, who was reportedly shot dead by suspected kidnappers at the Federal University of Technology, Owerri, FUTO, Imo State.

The incident occurred on Sunday, September 6, 2026, within the university premises, while the banker, who was based in Owerri, was reportedly taking his children to the institution.

Two female students were also reportedly abducted during the incident.

In a statement issued on Tuesday and signed by the Head, Brand Management and Corporate Communication of Polaris Bank, Rasheed Bolarinwa, the bank said the deceased was attacked by hoodlums while taking his children to the university.

The bank said his children managed to escape, but he was killed in the incident.

“We are deeply saddened by the tragic death of our Branch Manager and extend our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, colleagues, and loved ones during this difficult time.

“The unfortunate incident occurred on Sunday, when he was accosted by the hoodlums, and while the children managed to escape from the scene, he was not that lucky,” the statement said.

The bank said the incident was being investigated by relevant law enforcement agencies and expressed confidence that the circumstances surrounding the killing would be established.

“Our thoughts and prayers remain with the family of the deceased, and we respectfully urge the public to allow the authorities to complete their investigations,” it added.

Meanwhile, the management of FUTO confirmed that a visitor to the university was fatally shot during the incident and that two female students were reportedly abducted.

In a statement signed by the Registrar, Chinonso Uba, the university said the incident occurred on Sunday, adding that the circumstances were under investigation by security agencies.

“Management is engaging with the appropriate authorities regarding the safe recovery of the students,” the statement said.

The university assured students, staff, parents and other members of the community that their safety remained a priority, adding that additional security measures were being implemented in collaboration with security agencies.

It urged members of the university community to remain calm and vigilant, avoid unnecessary movement and promptly report suspicious activities.

Following the incident, FUTO management met with the Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, on Monday over security concerns around the university and its host communities.

Bosso reportedly assured the university management of intensified security around the institution and neighbouring communities, particularly the Ihiagwa, Eziobodo, Obinze and Nekede axes.

Meanwhile, a source who spoke on condition of anonymity said a proposed peaceful protest by some students over the killing was cancelled following the university’s reaffirmation of its ban on unruly and rowdy gatherings after examinations.

The ban was adopted by the FUTO Senate at its 495th and 501st meetings held on August 31, 2023, and April 29, 2024, respectively, following concerns over the destruction of university property, particularly during celebrations by graduating students.

The university management reaffirmed the prohibition at its seventh meeting held on Monday, September 7, 2026, warning students against activities capable of disrupting peace on the campus and in neighbouring communities.

The prohibited activities include rowdy behaviour, public revelry, disorderly conduct, littering, indiscriminate disposal of waste, blocking or obstructing roads and entrances, and damaging or defacing university property.

The management also warned against any conduct capable of threatening the safety and security of the university community.

World.title: Contractor Says His Barge, Not Nembe E&P Caused ‘Minor’ Bayelsa Vessel Accident
World.content:
•Dismisses claims of operational failure of oil firm’s equipment

•Says his vessel struck debris during movement

•Describes incident as ‘small’

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





Fresh details have emerged over the reported barge accident at the Nembe Creek facility in Bayelsa State, with the owner of the vessel involved in the incident revealing that it was caused by a minor mishap involving his barge.

He explained that the incident was in no way connected to the operations of Nembe Exploration and Production Ltd., formerly Aiteo Eastern Exploration and Production Ltd, contrary to some media reports.

Principal of Fazal Environmental Company, Mr Ebikeme Sokere, in a chat with THISDAY yesterday said the vessel was moving when it struck a broken block or debris, resulting in the incident, which he described as ‘minor’.

He specifically rejected any suggestion that Nembe Exploration or its predecessor, Aiteo, was responsible for the accident, stressing that the vessel belonged to his company and was not an operational crude-loading asset of the oil producer.

“It wasn’t really a big issue. It was a small accident. It wasn’t a serious matter. The barge was moving, then it hit a broken block or debris,” Sokere said. “It had nothing to do with Aiteo. It’s my barge, nothing to do with Aiteo,” he added.

His account is significant as the incident had initially been linked by the communities to crude-loading activities at the Nembe Creek facility operated by Nembe Exploration within Oil Mining Lease (OML) 29.

Environmental concerns surrounding the incident were heightened after the Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF) said it visited communities in the area and reported crude oil in waterways and along mangrove banks.

HOMEF subsequently demanded immediate cleanup, compensation for affected residents and full accountability, citing complaints from fishing communities over damaged equipment, reduced catches and restricted access to fishing grounds.

But the account from the vessel owner, supported by sources familiar with the incident, presented a different picture of what happened and the identity of the party responsible, with the vessel involved being a contractor’s remediation barge deployed for activities separate from Nembe Exploration’s crude production and evacuation operations.

Persons familiar with the incident described it as misleading any attempt to directly associate the incident with Nembe Exploration’s crude-loading operations without first establishing the contractual relationship, operational assignment and circumstances under which the barge was deployed.

“This is just very misleading. Nembe Exploration and Production Limited has no business with whatever happened to that barge. Whoever made that assertion needs to check again,” a person familiar with the incident said.

Sokere, for his part, said he was prepared to provide additional information to Nembe Exploration or other interested parties seeking to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident.

“If Aiteo needs me to come and explain to these people, I will come. It was a small incident, not a major issue,” he said, expressing surprise that such a minor incident was being blown out of proportion.

He also offered to take interested representatives to the location where the incident occurred, saying an inspection of the site would make the circumstances clearer. “If you come anytime or any of your representatives can come, I will show them to the place,” he said.

Sokere further emphasised that the barge was his company’s property, dismissing any suggestion that it was an asset belonging to Aiteo or Nembe Exploration.

“It was my barge. The name has an Izon name meaning ‘my heart is my refuge’. These are my people,” he said.

But HOMEF had demanded an assessment, which it said should be followed by compensation for verified economic and livelihood losses, particularly for fishing households whose nets, fishing equipment and access to fishing grounds were affected.

According to HOMEF, the incident spread through interconnected waterways as a result of tidal movements, raising concerns among communities that depend substantially on fishing for food and income.

Vice-Chair of Nembe Creek women, Mrs Love Mark, specifically said residents were struggling to replace damaged fishing equipment.

HOMEF Executive Director, Dr Nnimmo Bassey, had also called for affected communities and fishing camps to be incorporated into investigations, damage assessments, cleanup and subsequent environmental monitoring.

World.title: Shelton Beats Alcaraz in Late-night ‘War’ to Reach Semis
World.content:
Carlos Alcaraz’s US Open title defence came to an end in a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton which ended at 03:34 local time – the latest finish in the tournament’s history.

A large crowd remained captivated deep into the night as a modern classic unfolded over an unpredictable four hours and 28 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

The match did not begin until about 11pm in New York, after the start of the night session was delayed by Tuesday’s earlier matches.

At its conclusion, eighth seed Shelton basked in a standing ovation from a delirious audience after completing a 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) victory that will live long in the memory of all those present.

“That was a war, an epic match, so physical,” Shelton said.

“Carlos is one of the greatest champions in our sport already at 23 years old.

“It’s ridiculous some of the stuff he comes up with sometimes – the most enjoyable match that I’ve had in my career, for sure.”

This was the biggest – and certainly most significant – win of Shelton’s career.

He had not beaten a top-three player in 17 attempts, and had lost each of his three previous matches against Spain’s Alcaraz.

It also boosted home hopes of a first American men’s singles champion in New York for 23 years.

Shelton was less than a year old when Andy Roddick won the US Open in 2003 – but an American finalist is guaranteed when he and Frances Tiafoe meet in Friday’s semi-finals.

World number three Alcaraz was competing at his first tournament since a lengthy injury lay-off, but that is to take nothing away from Shelton, who produced a phenomenal performance.

Seven-time major winner Alcaraz had exceeded expectations on his return after more than four months out with a wrist injury, including sweeping past 20th seed Tommy Paul to reach the last eight.

But the 23-year-old’s lack of match fitness appeared to finally catch up with him in a high-octane encounter filled with breathless exchanges and astounding displays of athleticism.

Even when it appeared Alcaraz had emptied the tank, the two-time winner not only forced a deciding set but would go the distance as the players engaged in a tense 10-point match tie-break that provided a fitting conclusion to the contest.

“It was close. So I’m just not going to be disappointed about not getting the win at the end,” said Alcaraz.

“I’m just proud about myself, about how I fought. I leave the court with a smile, healthy, and this is what I needed.”

World.title: Ochei Hails Ogunsakin as Nigerian Ends 35-year Grand Slam Jinx
World.content:
President of the Nigeria Tennis Federation (NTF), Rt. Hon. Victor O. Ochei Esq, FNSE, has hailed the historic feat of young Nigerian tennis sensation, Seun Ogunsakin, who has broken a 35-year Grand Slam drought for Nigeria.

Ogunsakin made history at the Junior US Open in New York, becoming the first Nigerian player to win a Grand Slam main draw singles match – across both professional and junior draws – since tennis legend Nduka Odizor achieved the feat at the 1990 Australian Open.

The feat is even more remarkable as Ogunsakin is listed among Africa’s Next Gen, where for the first time since 2003, three boys from African nations reached the main draw at the US Open Junior Championships.

Reacting to the development, Engr. Ochei, who assumed office as NTF President with a mandate to reposition Nigerian tennis, described Ogunsakin’s victory as a vindication of the reforms and grassroots investment of his board.

“This is another monumental feat since we assumed office. After our historic records in the Davis Cup and the Billie Jean King Cup qualifiers, Ogunsakin has done it again. He has ended a 35-year wait since our legend Nduka Odizor. This is not luck, this is the result of deliberate work, of believing in our young talents and giving them a platform,” Ochei said.

“On behalf of the Board of the Nigeria Tennis Federation, I congratulate Ogunsakin for his courage, discipline and brilliance. He has shown that Nigerian tennis is back on the global map. This is what we promised – to take tennis from the streets of Nigeria to the centre court of the world. And we are just starting.”

The NTF President noted that under his leadership, the Federation has prioritized junior development, international exposure, and private sector partnership, including the support for national championships like the DAVNOTCH Open as a deliberate strategy to breed champions.

He dedicated the victory to all young Nigerian players in academies across the country, urging them to see Ogunsakin’s story as proof that Grand Slam dreams are valid.

Ogunsakin is expected to continue his campaign in the main draw of the US Open Junior Championships.

World.title: MFM, Customs, ASO SKY, Victoria Queens Secure Zenith Bank League Final 8 Slots

World.title: Nigeria’s Ambassador in Poland Backs Falconets for Victory against China Today
World.content:
Ahead of Falconets’ clash with China at the ongoing 2026 FIFA U20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, Nigeria’s Ambassador to that country, Ambassador Margareta Mary Obi, has urged the team to put their opening match defeat by Spain behind and stay focused of winning today.

The two-time silver-medallists will take to the pitch of the Stadion Sosnowiec for their second match this evening in a must-win encounter against China

The Chinese girls are highly motivated after a 5-0 pounding of New Caledonia in their first match – a result that has established them at the top of the Group F table, ahead of 2022 champions Spain on goals difference.

But the Nigerian envoy reminded Falconets that they played good football and have every reason to remain confident against the Chinese ladies.

The ambassador did not abandon the team or feel dejected like everyone else despite the defeat against Spain last Monday.

She watched the match played at the Stadion Sosnowiec, and alongside mission staff, did her best to support and encourage the team.

After the game, Ambassador Mary Obi took time to interact with the players and technical crew, encouraging the girls not to be discouraged by their opening defeat to Spain.

In a thoughtful gesture, the top diplomat also brought Nigerian food for the players, helping to lift the mood and give the team a taste of home while away in Poland. Her presence and words of encouragement provided a timely morale boost as the Falconets turn their attention to their crucial clash with China.

Coach Moses Aduku said on Wednesday night: “We have put the match against Spain behind us and focussing totally on the clash with China. The players are ready to come out stronger for the match against China.”

Nigeria and China have met twice previously at the FIFA U20 Women’s World Cup finals.

In 2006 in Russia – the very competition where the event was renamed FIFA U20 (as against U19 for the two first tournaments in Canada and Thailand), China defeated the Falconets 3-0 in a group phase match at the Podmoskovie Stadium.

In 2018 in France, a late own goal by a Chinese defender handed Nigeria a 1-1 draw in their match in Dinan-Léhon – a result that sent the Falconets into the tournament’s quarterfinals.

World.title: Facts Emerge How FG’s N17bn Intervention Funding Given to NFF Was Used to Settle Debts
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

In apparent reply to claims by the leadership of the National Sports Commission (NSC) that the immediate past board of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) received better funding from the Federal Government than any other previous board of the football federation, a former member of that executive committee insisted yesterday that it will be wrong to treat the N17billion intervention money given to the sacked board in isolation and also as evidence of financial wrongdoings.

Chairman of the NSC, Malam Shehu Dikko, while appearing on AriseNews sports programme at the weekend, made comparison between the funding received by the Ibrahim Gusau-led NFF board with that of his predecessor, Amaju Melvin Pinnick.

Dikko concluded that the N17billion intervention funds released in a single cheque to the Gusau-led board was far greater than the about N15billion in total that Pinnick got in his eight years tenure as NFF president between 2014 and 2022.

The NSC chairman had used the comparison to drum for accountability and the need for reforms in the administration of football in Nigeria.

But a member of that board who craved to be anonymous due to the ongoing investigations into the finances of the NFF by anti-graft agencies, said that

the Gusau-led board inherited huge financial debts from the Pinnick administration.

“I don’t want to dispute that our board received the N17billion intervention funding from the Federal Government. There is a detailed account of how the money was applied, included settlement of prior liabilities,” began the influential member of that immediate board of the NFF.

He listed one of the huge debts inherited by the Gusau-led board to include

the 23-month backlog of Coach Jose Peseiro’s $70,000 USD monthly wage. “Peseiro’s unpaid salary alone gulped over a million dollars,” revealed the source.

Surprisingly, the former board member further alleged that the outstanding Peseiro’s salary was recorded as paid by the Pinnick board when Gusau took over.

“Unfortunately, this was one of the debts that the Gusau board inherited. The Pinnick board claimed that it was bankrolled by AITEO. We met it as debt. It was the Gusau board that settled it,” the source stressed.

While throwing further clarifications on how the intervention funds were spent, our top football source also listed the huge debts inherited from the Pinnick led board to include outstanding match allowances and bonuses due to Super Eagles players, and officials, some dating back to the qualifiers for the 2018 FIFA World Cup that held in Russia.

The former board member said that Dikko who was a second vice president of the Pinnick led NFF board should not be economical with the truth as he is much aware of the huge debt they left for the Gusau board to inherit.

“As it is usually the case, any one seeking equity must come with clean hands. Is Dikko exonerating himself from the huge debts left by the board where he was a vice president?” queried the source.

“I want to make it clear that receiving more funding than a previous administration isn’t, by itself, evidence of anything impropriety. Rather, the question that matters is how the cash were applied. Without any contradiction, the Gusau-led board used major part of that N17bn fund to clear the debts left behind by the Pinnick and Dikko led board.”

He was emphatic in stating that the exchange rate in place during the Gusau era made things difficult for the board. “When Pinnick was in office, dollar exchanged for between N200 to N600 to a dollar. But Gusau got N17 billion at the time one dollar was exchanging to Naira at N1,500. So technically, it will not be wrong to say that the N15billion that Pinnick got during his time as NFF President was greater than the N17billion given to the Gusau led board when dollar was going for N1,500,” concludes the former board member.

World.title: NSC Confirms Payment of Presidential Rewards of $100,000 each to D’Tigresses
World.content:
*Insists Super Falcons to also get their rewards next month

Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The National Sports Commission (NSC) has officially confirmed the payment of Naira equivalent of $100,000 (about N133million) to D’Tigresses and $50,000 (about N66.5million) to the team officials being President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR’s cash reward to the team for winning the 2025 FIBA Women’s Afrobasket for a record fifth consecutive time and seventh overall.

According to a statement issued yesterday by the NSC’s Director of Information, Dr. Kehinde Ajayi, the players and officials’ accounts were credited on Wednesday, September 9th 2026 and they have all confirmed the receipt of the same.

This comes after the team’s last match at the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup in Germany where they failed to make it to the quarterfinal stage after losing all three group games.

With the payment, the entire presidential rewards promised to each member of the team by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR comprising a 3-Bedroom flat in Abuja, national honours of OON and Naira equivalent of 100,000 USD to players and 50,000 USD to officials have been fully redeemed and completed.

“Players and officials of the D’Tigresses had, in February 2026 in Lyon, France during the FIBA World Cup qualifiers received from the National Sports Commission the title documents (C of O) of their 3-bedroom apartments in Abuja and certificates of national honours of OON duly signed by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu GCFR.

“Similarly, the Super Falcons had received from the NSC the title documents (C of O) to their 3-Bedroom apartments in Abuja as well as certificates of national honours of OON duly signed by the President/C-in-C during the last Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) in Morroco in July/August 2026.

“Like the D’Tigresses, the Super Falcons should get the alerts for the Naira equivalent of 100,000 USD to players and 50,000 USD to the officials before their next official engagements to complete their presidential rewards as well,” the NSC spokesperson stated in the statement.

Super Falcons had been feted by President Tinubu for winning the WAFCON for the 10th time in Morocco in 2025 with 3-Bedroom flats in Abuja, national honours of OON and Naira equivalent of 100,000 USD to players and 50,000 USD to Officials.

This unprecedented reward to the players and athletes by the Federal Government of Nigeria, is in alignment with the Renewed Hope initiative and Shared Prosperity agenda of President Tinubu which places athletes’ welfare and appropriate rewards top on the priority list.

“On behalf of the entire players and officials of D’Tigresses, Super Falcons and Super Eagles, the National Sports Commission thanks Mr. President for his immense support and unwavering support for Nigerian sports, as well as his commitment to positioning the sector as an instrument of national development and social/economic advancement, which has given impetus to the Commission’s reform agenda in the pursuit of a sustainable sports economy in line with the Renewed Hope Initiative for Nigeria’s Sports Economy (RHINSE) framework,” Mrs Ajayi concluded in the NSC statement.

The Commission also expresses its gratitude to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, the Minister of the FCT, the Minister of Housing and Urban Development, the Minister of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs and Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation for the support and collaboration with NSC to ensure Mr. President’s rewards to the teams were duly implemented in record time within the due process requirements.

World.title: Champions League: Odegaard Fires Arsenal Winner at Napoli
World.content:
Martin Odegaard’s excellent start to the season continued as the Arsenal captain came to his side’s rescue against Napoli in Naples. The Gunners won 1-0.

The Gunners were guilty of wasteful finishing and were heading for a frustrating draw in their first game in the Champions League since losing last season’s final in agonising fashion.

However, Odegaard had Arsenal’s 1,500 travelling fans celebrating after a fine finish from outside the box – the captain’s fourth goal in five games, including the Community Shield.

Piero Hincapie dropped to his knees after the full-time whistle and thumped the ground with his hands in relief at the result.

Arsenal won all eight group phase games on their way to last season’s final, and they are up and running after a fine win in Italy.

Mikel Arteta’s side had missed three great chances to punish last season’s Serie A runners-up before Odegaard’s winner.

There were 29 passes in the build-up to Arsenal’s winner, their second-most on record (since 2003-04) for a Champions League goal (33 for Lucas Perez’s second at Basel in December 2016).

World.title: Anele Mdoda’s wedding show coming to Netflix
World.content:
Anele Mdoda is set to share more of her love story in her upcoming Netflix wedding docu-soap.

South African media and radio personality Anele Mdoda will give fans a closer look at her journey to the altar in a new Netflix wedding docu-soap.

Titled Stars & Vows: Anele and Buzza, the upcoming series will follow Mdoda and her husband, Bonelela “Buzza James” Mgudlwa, as they navigate their relationship and married life in the spotlight.

Netflix has confirmed that the series will premiere later in 2026, although the streaming platform has not announced an exact release date.



Dopezuluboi Productions produced the project, which will stream exclusively on Netflix.

ANELE MDODA’S LOVE STORY HEADS TO NETFLIX

The streaming giant has already given viewers a glimpse of what they can expect from the highly anticipated series.

According to Netflix, “Stars and Vows: Anele & Buzza | Coming Soon | From a budding romance to bridal bliss under the bright lights of fame, Stars and Vows: Anele & Buzza follows the love story of TV & radio personality Anele Mdoda and Bonelela “Buzza James” Mgudlwa as they navigate the challenges, joy and anticipation on the road to saying “I do.”



“The documentary soap and wedding special is created by Nomzamo Mbatha, Teddy Geldart, Vuyo Sowah and Pet Tasara, and directed by Pascual Wakefield. The series is set to launch on Netflix later this year.”

Anele has also confirmed the project herself, teasing fans about what is coming.

“Okay Guys. You guys are getting the visuals,” she said.



The announcement has already sparked excitement among fans who will now get to see a more personal side of the media personality.

Okay guys.



You are getting the visuals 😍 pic.twitter.com/0jC7TK1GJ3 — Anele Mdoda (@Anele) September 9, 2026

A STAR-STUDDED CREATIVE TEAM

The production brings together several prominent names from South Africa’s entertainment industry.



Actress and producer Nomzamo Mbatha is among the creators, alongside Teddy Geldart, Vuyo Sowah and Pet Tasara. Pascual Wakefield directs the series.

Bright Fire Productions also confirmed the project in a joint post with Anele, describing the production as a celebration of their relationship.

“Two souls. Two worlds. One extraordinary love story



Stars and Vows: Anele and Buzza is a beautiful reminder that sometimes love doesn’t arrive quietly — it arrives boldly, beautifully and completely unapologetically. A union of royal hearts and rebellious spirits, choosing each other, choosing love and choosing a life written beyond the rules.

Stars and Vows: Anele and Buzza.”

The production company’s statement highlights the couple’s journey while teasing the emotional story that viewers can expect when the series arrives.



ANELE MDODA’S WEDDING ROOTED IN XHOSA TRADITION

Mdoda and Buzza exchanged vows on 20 April 2025 in a vibrant ceremony that celebrated Xhosa culture and tradition.

Their wedding brought together love, family and heritage, making it a memorable chapter in their relationship.



Now, more than a year after their wedding, viewers will have the opportunity to see more of the journey behind the celebration.

Mdoda marked their first wedding anniversary on 20 April 2026 with a heartfelt tribute to her husband.

“Andonwabe. One year later my love @buzza_james thank you for the safest yet wildest fire of love. God loves us if he keeps doing it like this with us. My royal rebel.”



Her message offered fans another glimpse into the bond she shares with Buzza as they celebrated their first year of marriage.

FANS WILL SEE THE STORY BEHIND THE CELEBRATION

While the couple has already shared moments of their relationship publicly, Stars & Vows: Anele and Buzza promises to take audiences much further behind the scenes.



The series will explore the anticipation, emotions and traditions surrounding their wedding while showing the couple navigating a major chapter in their lives.

For fans of Mdoda, the project also offers an opportunity to see her away from her familiar television and radio roles.

The combination of romance, family, culture and celebrity is expected to make the series an interesting watch for Netflix audiences.



Stars & Vows: Anele and Buzza is scheduled to arrive on Netflix later in 2026. An official premiere date is still to be announced.

World.title: Checkers brings back discontinued chocolate – for now
World.content:
Checkers has quietly reintroduced a discontinued chocolate brand – Nestle’s Caravan – back onto shelves – for a limited period.

CHECKERS BRINGS BACK CARAVAN CHOCOLATE!

A week ago, Checkers polled its customers on which discontinued chocolate it should bring back to shelves. The options included: Beacon’s New Look and FFWD, Nestle’s Caravan and Cadbury’s 7777.

Although they did not reveal the poll results, consumers have reported finding the Chocolate bar, paired with Nestle’s Tex, on their shelves.



In a viral post, the Facebook page called 1986 Stories shared: “THIS IS NOT A DRILL 🚨🚨. The Caravan Chocolate is back! I bought this today, 7 September, at Checkers [for] R15.99”

According to the Shoprite Group, to which Checkers falls, the chocolate is back as a special-edition offering.

DISCONTINUED TREATS IN SOUTH AFRICA

Caravan was quietly discontinued long before the Covid-19 pandemic hit. According to Nestle, this was to make room for new product offerings.



The chocolate is one of many sweet treats that have ceased production and can no longer be found on shelves.

Others include Nestle’s Chocolate Log, Cadbury’s Tempo, Inside Story, FFWD, and Holey Moleys.

Other household products have also been given the chop – from Nesquik to TaB to Redro Fish Paste andHellmann’s mayonnaise.

World.title: ‘What Duba told me before I scored that freekick’ – Kaizer Chiefs new signing
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs’ newest signing, Faiz Abrahams has revealed what happened before he scored the freekick against Siwelele on Sunday.

Amakhosi won 3-2 at the Dobsonville Stadium and Abrahams was one of the scorers after a sublime freekick.

Leading 2-1, Chiefs were awarded a free kick in the 76th minute deep inside Siwelele territory, roughly midway between the left touchline and the penalty area. The new Amakhosi man lined up to take it and it seem he was going to cross it but went for goal.



“When I went to take the free kick, (Wandile) Duba told me not to cross the ball for anyone but to try and score,” Abrahams was quoted on Kaizer Chiefs website.

“It felt great because I have been working very hard,” he added

“I’m just going to keep working hard and giving my all in training. I aim to stay consistent and always keep my performance levels up.”



Kaizer Chiefs enjoying a good start to the season

After impressing this past weekend, Abrahams will look to maintain the same performance as Chiefs travel to Polokwane City on Saturday

“The coach will set a plan for this weekend, and we will go out and execute it,” he said.

The Betway Premiership encounter between Polokwane City and Kaizer Chiefs kicks off at 15:00 on Saturday, 12 September, at the old Peter Mokaba stadium. A win for the Glamour Boys will see them jump into second place on the log ahead of rivals Orlando Pirates.

World.title: Anele Tembe inquest: AKA ordered tequila, hotel said ‘NO’
World.content:
AKA and his entourage reportedly ordered tequila shooters after the death of his fiancee, Anele Tembe at the Pepperclub Hotel in 2021. Images via IG

A manager at the Pepperclub Hotel in Cape Town testified how they refused to serve rapper AKA – real name Kiernan Forbes – and his entourage tequila shooters after the death of his fiancée Anele Tembe just hours earlier. The testimony was heard during an inquest at the Cape Town Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday.

Anele fell to her death from the 10th-floor balcony on 11 April 2021. According to witnesses, the couple had argued in their hotel room moments before her death.

Tragically, AKA was shot and killed by masked gunmen in Durban two years later.



ANELE TEMBE INQUEST: AKA DENIED TEQUILA SHOTS

On Wednesday, the inquest into Anele Tembe’s death continued, with the court hearing how a male hotel manager had refused to serve tequila shooters to a room occupied by AKA and his entourage.

The group placed the order at around 9:00 am, a little over an hour after Anele had fallen off her 10th-floor hotel balcony to her death on the pavement below. AKA did not go down to the ground floor to see Anele, but had remained in a neighbouring hotel room. A witness came to Anele’s aid, testifying how he had comforted and prayed over her until emergency services arrived.

The manager – whose identity was one of multiple witnesses the court ruled should remain private – told the court that the group had subsequently ordered alcohol, but he had refused to serve it.

He said, “I said it was not something we should entertain. They were not happy about the restrictions, and I had to speak to them.”

ANELE TEMBE INQUEST:



A hotel manager has told the inquest into Tembe’s death that staff stopped serving alcohol to her fiancé, the late rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes, after she fell to her death from the hotel’s 10th floor @NtuthuzeloNene — EWN Reporter (@ewnreporter) September 9, 2026

He said AKA and the others were unhappy with the restriction, but that the rapper did not become notably angry or upset.



A hotel guest corroborated the claims, testifying that “it did not make sense”, given what had happened moments earlier in the hotel room.

THE GRUESOME HOTEL ROOM

Also heard during the inquest was a detailed account of the evidence found in AKA and Anele Tembe’s hotel room.

According to a police investigator, the room was a “mess”, and evidence found suggested a physical struggle. This included a bloodied champagne bottle, blood on bed linen, towels and on a wall.

The room was also strewn with cans and cigarette butts.

A chair near the balcony was also found, with the investigator claiming that AKA had stated that Anele had climbed over the railing and jumped to her death. However, the Tembe family lawyer questioned why Anele’s fingerprints were not found on the railing.

The investigator shared that AKA had insisted on making a police statement shortly after Anele’s fall.

He told the court of his interaction with the rapper: “He didn’t look any sad or anything like that. He looked, to be honest, looked quite fine.

“I’ve dealt with a lot of cases with people that will cry, and some people will be [sitting] still, don’t talk to you at all. He looked quite fine to me, to be honest.”

ANELE TEMBE’S DAD: ‘WHO DOES THAT?

In 2024, author Melinda Ferguson published her book, When Love Kills, A Tragic Tale about AKA and Anele. In it, Anele Tembe’s father, Moses, questioned AKA’s actions following his daughter’s balcony fall.

He said in the book: “Who doesn’t go down and try to help the woman he loves when he sees her lying in the street?

“No one who saw the body of the woman they loved wouldn’t have rushed down to help her. She wasn’t dead.

“When Rob Stefanutto [an eyewitness] approached Anele, she responded by blinking. Within minutes of seeing his fiancée lying on the road, Kiernan orders tequila. Who does that?”

World.title: Full-time score: Mamelodi Sundowns 3-0 Siwelele FC
World.content:
Sundowns had to remain patient after a goalless first half. They eventually found their breakthrough through Kutlwano Letlhaku shortly after the interval.

The result takes the African champions six points clear at the summit.

Siwelele FC remain without a win after another difficult night for the managerless side.



MAMELODI SUNDOWNS BREAK SIWELELE RESISTANCE

Siwelele frustrated the hosts during the opening 45 minutes as caretaker coach Godfrey Mosoetsa set up his team to defend in numbers.

Sundowns controlled much of the possession and territory but struggled to find a way through a disciplined Siwelele defence.

Goalkeeper Tshigwana Gift Mthombeni also produced a solid performance between the posts as the visitors managed to keep the reigning champions at bay.

The two teams went into the halftime break locked at 0-0, with Khulumani Ndamane picking up the only booking for Sundowns in the opening period in Tshwane.

Cardoso eventually turned to his bench for fresh energy and the decision paid off.

In the 58th minute, Kutlwano Letlhaku broke the deadlock for Sundowns, with the goal confirmed after a VAR check.



The goal changed the complexion of the match as Sundowns gained greater control and forced Siwelele FC to chase the game.

Mosoetsa responded with changes of his own, introducing Hamza Issah and Thato Letshedi, but the visitors could not find a way past Ronwen Williams.

SIYANDA NDLOVU INSPIRES LATE ROUT

Sundowns eventually made their superior squad depth count in the closing stages.

Siyanda Ndlovu, wearing number 38 after coming off the bench, doubled the advantage in the 79th minute with a superb finish to put Sundowns firmly in control.

Siwelele were unable to respond as the game entered stoppage time, and Ndlovu then produced another decisive moment.

The Sundowns substitute turned provider with an excellent through ball for Tashreeq Matthews, who showed composure to produce a clinical lob over the goalkeeper and make it 3-0.

Also read: Transfer report: Sundowns beat Pirates to sign Bafana star Matuludi

The final whistle confirmed another important victory for Sundowns, who continue to set the pace at the top of the Betway Premiership.

For Siwelele, however, the difficult start to the campaign continues, with the club still searching for its first victory.

World.title: 'Jou ma se ****' - Pemmy Majodina loses cool during community engagement
World.content:
KOUGA - Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina's meeting with the Kouga community descended into chaos.

Profanities were exchanged between Majodina and a community member during a launch of an upgraded pump station.

This was a dramatic turn of events which left the community in shock.

A community member who was being escorted out of the venue said "jou ma se ****" to Majodina and she responded by saying "Phuma! Jou ma se **** ook."

eNCA spoke to Kyle Minnaar, an administrator in the Kouga Municipality, who detailed the heated meeting with the community.

According to Minnaar, the day started with the launch before moving to government community engagement.

Minnaar said, two serious concerns came out of that meeting, the first being that the meeting was heavily politicised and the second was the chaos which erupted.

“During the Q&A session, a resident who was forced out of the hall was disagreeing with another resident who was talking. I suppose he talked out of turn when the Minister requested that this resident be removed from the hall. Whilst he was walking out of the hall, she passed the insult.”

Minnaar said he was disappointed with the Minister.

He said while he notes that the community member who was escorted out may have been guilty of speaking out of turn, but that is not enough reason for the Minister to respond in that manner.

World.title: Evacuations in Malibu after waves open sinkhole at Nicolas Cage's house
World.content:
MALIBU - People living in an upmarket coastal stretch of Malibu were under an evacuation order Wednesday after a giant sinkhole opened up on the driveway of a beachfront home belonging to Oscar-winning US actor Nicolas Cage.

The enormous hole appeared Tuesday as heavy surf, brought by the after-effects of a hurricane, pounded the exclusive coastline, which is home to some of California's wealthiest people and a host of celebrities.

Photographs of the crater, estimated to be as much as 60 feet (18 meters) wide in places, showed it contained concrete, tiles and a portable toilet that appeared to have been placed at the multi-million dollar home for use by workmen who were doing alterations.

By Tuesday evening, the sinkhole was around 25 feet deep, as waves from the churning Pacific Ocean continued to eat away at the coastline, lapping around the stanchions that support the house which the "Leaving Las Vegas" actor bought for $10.5 million.

Malibu city officials issued an evacuation order affecting dozens of homes in some of the most sought-after real estate in Southern California.

"The Director of Emergency Services of the City of Malibu has declared the existence of a local emergency following a large sinkhole forming near 31630 Sea Level Drive," an announcement said.

"An evacuation order is in effect for all affected properties. Sheriff Deputies have notified residents in person, and a digital alert has been issued by the City."

South of Los Angeles, truckloads of boulders had been placed along a stretch of beach in Dana Point in an effort to protect properties in a spot where seven homes have already been declared uninhabitable, with one partially collapsing into the sea.

Richard Thompson, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, told AFP on Tuesday that coastal waters were being roiled by the remnants of Hurricane Marie.

"There were some pretty significant surf and swells across area in the last several days," he said.

"At the height of the surf and swell, we had some very significant wave heights of 10 up to 15 feet (3.0-4.5 meters) in some spots, along with significant beach erosion."

This week Hurricane Lowell lashed Hawaii with damaging winds, heavy rainfall and powerful floods, blacking out power across most of one island.

A near-record-strength El Nino climate episode is warming the waters of the Pacific Ocean and promoting the formation of powerful storms.

While the warming phase is a natural phenomenon, scientists believe the human-caused heating of the climate could make its effects much larger.

World.title: Lower electricity prices, jobs creation: Ramaphosa makes promises in Thembisa

THEMBISA - ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa said government is working to ease pressure on households, while attracting investment and creating jobs.

Speaking on the campaign trail in Thembisa, he acknowledged that weak economic growth remains a challenge.

Ramaphosa said measures are being put in place to bring down electricity prices and grow the economy.

"That is why we are embarking on restructuring of our electricity sector so that prices can be brought down on an overall basis," Ramaphosa said.

He also noted concerns over unemployment, but Ramaphosa said efforts are being made to attract investment to make sure that the economy grows.

World.title: '800 000 mandrax tablets produced a day': Hawks uncover drug lab in Pretoria
World.content:
PREOTRIA - Hawks have cracked a drug syndicate after pouncing on another drug lab, this time in Erasmia, west of Pretoria.

The lab is said to have allegedly been producing approximately 800 000 mandrax tablets a day.

Added to this, police believe this is also the discovery of a new establishment that purports to be manufacturing crystal meth.

READ | R800,000 cocaine haul lands man in custody at OR Tambo

According to Deputy National Commissioner for Policing Tebello Mosikili, two foreign nationals were arrested during the raid on the clandestine mandrax lab and drugs were seized.

“This is a major blow to a large-scale criminal syndicate and to the illicit drug supply chain in South Africa. Eight hundred thousand tablets a day is not just a small number. “By dismantling this facility, we are disrupting the production capacity of a network capable of flooding our communities with hundreds of thousands of mandrax tablets every single day,” Mosikili said.

According to Mosikili, the operation was intelligence-led, with crime intelligence having monitored activities and movements at this small holding for some time.

She said authorities are now working on establishing the source of the drugs.

World.title: Unless doctor says otherwise, Mapisa-Nqakula trial unlikely to derail - Expert
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A legal expert believes former Defence Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula's corruption trial is unlikely to be marred by postponements.

Melusi Xulu said proceedings should continue as scheduled unless Mapisa-Nqakula's doctors argue otherwise.

“The foundation of a criminal trial, which is based on the Constitution, says there must be a fair trial. So, if you're not feeling well, it's important that the court takes cognisance of that and then you are given time, obviously, to recuperate and be in a better condition. But most possibly a doctor's note will be sufficient,” he said.

Xulu’s comments come as the High Court in Pretoria adjourned its proceedings earlier than expected after Mapisa-Nqakula required medical attention following a full day in the witness stand.

Her lawyer requested an early adjournment, citing Mapisa-Nqakula's fatigue.

READ | Lawyer says Mapisa-Nqakula is 'just tired'

At the time, lawyers attributed the tiredness possibly to the lengthy court process, which can be "gruelling, tiring and frustrating" for someone not used to it.

Xulu said while such an explanation could be valid, a medical proof would be enough for the court to decide if the matter warrants a postponement to a time when she is better state and ready to face the court as directed by the doctor.

Mapisa-Nqakula faces 12 charges of corruption and one of money laundering.

These are linked to allegations that she solicited and received millions of rands in bribes, while serving as Defence Minister.

READ | Mapisa-Nqakula denies 'code words' for alleged bribes

The former minister admitted that defence contractor Nombasa Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu visited her home, but said they discussed a family matter.

She denied soliciting or receiving bribes from Ntsondwa-Ndhlovu.

Mapisa-Nqakula's lawyer said they will await confirmation from the doctors to decide on Thursday's proceedings.

This communication, he said, is expected to happen before the end of the day on Wednesday.

World.title: ODI debutant Hermann scores 150 as Proteas beat Namibia
World.content:
WINDHOEK - Jordan Hermann scored 150 on Wednesday in his one-day international debut for South Africa, which beat Namibia by 99 runs in a rain-shortened first ODI between the countries.

Opener Hermann and Tony de Zorzi put on 190 for the second wicket in Windhoek and the visitors posted 348-6 off 50 overs after being put in to bat.

Rain forced two interruptions to the Namibia reply and, set 262 in 31 overs to win under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method, they could only reach 162-8.

It has been a memorable four days for left-hand batter Hermann, whose career-best Twenty20 knock of 53 on Sunday helped South Africa win a tri-series final against Zimbabwe in Namibia.

After fellow opener Connor Esterhuizen fell for 10, Hermann and De Zorzi tormented the Namibian bowlers at one of the venues for the 2027 ODI Men's Cricket World Cup.

Hermann faced 126 deliveries and hit three sixes and 17 fours. The 72 runs of De Zorzi included a six and seven fours.

A soft, lofted shot by Hermann off South Africa-born quick Ruben Trumpelmann proved his undoing as Louren Steenkamp took a catch at extra cover.

De Zorzi was trapped leg before by Gerhard Erasmus after a long appeal and an even longer wait before the umpire raised his finger.

After a 51-run first wicket stand between Malan Kruger (34) and Alexander Busing-Volschenk (15), Namibia battled with spinner Prenelan Subrayen (4-29) inflicting most damage.

Brief scores

South Africa 348-6 in 50 overs (J. Hermann 150, T. de Zorzi 72; R. Trumpelmann 4-68) v Namibia 162-8 in 31 overs (M. Kruger 34, J.J. Smit 31; P. Subrayen 4-29, K. Maphaka 2-32)

Result: South Africa won by 99 runs under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method

Toss: Namibia

Series: South Africa lead 1-0 ahead of matches on Friday and Sunday

World.title: Rubio pushes extraditions, anti-drug fight in Ecuador
World.content:
WASHINGTON - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Ecuador Wednesday to press the fight against "narco-terrorists" who have transformed the country into one of Latin America's most violent.

Rubio visits Quito as the second stop on a three-nation tour designed to shore up conservative allies in Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, and bolster US influence across the continent.

He is expected to discuss tougher extradition rules for drug traffickers, push military operations against alleged drug-runners and champion investment from politically connected US tech firms like Google, Palantir and SpaceX.

On the eve of his visit, Rubio described Ecuador as "one of our closest security partners in the region, and I think there's more we can do with them."

A year ago, the US government dramatically shifted its anti-drug strategy to include air strikes against vessels suspected of shipping drugs in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific.

The strikes have killed more than 200 people, according to US Defense Department figures.

World.title: Airports Company South Africa back flying high
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Airports Company South Africa (ACSA) is benefiting from increased travel demand.

The state-owned airport operator, ACSA, which runs nine airports across the country, is showing solid growth.

It's reporting stronger annual earnings as passenger numbers continue to rise.

Growth in both its aviation and commercial businesses has helped lift performance.

Its revenue increased by 11.6% to R8.78 billion.

Passenger numbers are seeing a significant recovery, falling just 2% shy of pre-COVID levels.

However, the one thorn in the side of ACSA's success is jet fuel and labour costs.

These inputs have doubled over the last year.
