World.title: The problem with replatforming Alfred ‘Krip’ Yuson
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines – Filipino literature and the classics that have come out of it always deserve to be known, and it’s often made possible by efforts like republishing and circulating physical copies to make them accessible to even more readers. But when the author behind one of these books has caused more harm than good, it becomes an entirely different story.

Case in point: Alfred “Krip” Yuson and his 1988 novel Great Philippine Jungle Energy Café.

The book was supposed to have been given new life by Exploding Galaxies — with the publishing house even standing by its initial decision to republish the book despite drawing backlash from members of the literary community. Here’s what went down.

Yuson’s web of controversies

Yuson, a Carlos Palanca Memorial Awards for Literature Hall of Fame inductee, has been accused by several individuals of alleged sexual misconduct. His latest published work was the 2022 book The Mountain That Grew.

“Why re-platform a man who’s responsible for the harassment and suicide of women? I do not care how brilliant you think his book is. I DO NOT CARE. And I will NEVER understand,” writer Katrina Stuart Santiago said in a Threads post on August 26.

Santiago further attested that she knows of young female writers who have had their own share of “horrid” experiences at the hands of Yuson.

“I remember when writers were being ‘cancelled’ left and right for everything from minor indiscretions to horrible mistakes to bad decisions, my question then was: when do we talk about the dirty old men of the literary establishment? Because THAT is a list. And it also has a list of victims. Re-platforming one of them by reprinting his book seems like [a] signal, doesn’t it. Of many things, including that people think we forget who these men are. We do not. We cannot. WE SHOULD NOT,” she said in another post on August 27.

Santiago added that literary workshops fuel Yuson’s predatory behavior, given the power dynamics that exist in these spaces between mentors and their mentees.

In response, Exploding Galaxies had initially attempted to discredit Santiago’s commentary, stating that while sexual harassment isn’t something they take lightly, the allegations that have been thrown at Yuson “have not been proven or independently corroborated.”

“We republished Great Philippine Jungle Energy Café for its well-established literary merit, and we stand by our decision to publish the book,” Exploding Galaxies wrote in its first public statement on September 5.

“We also stand firm against dishonest and unfair attempts to discredit this republication, especially as it is coming from a person who has expressed a longstanding personal grudge against the author, and who has, over the years, leveled serious public accusations against others,” it added.

Public response

Other figures in the literary community were quick to weigh in on the matter, with award-winning writer Jose “Butch” Dalisay Jr. pondering on the topic of art being created by questionable individuals.

“Does moral or political purity translate to some kind of elevated prose, or more honest and insightful poetry?” he wrote in a Facebook post. “Can someone please put together a library of vetted literature (or otherwise a new Index Librorum Prohibitorium) to spare us the process, and so we can keep to the straight and narrow, and enjoy reading without guilt or shame?”

Dalisay had followed it up with another post apologizing for appearing to trivialize the plight of sexual harassment victims — adding that the phenomenon of enabling a culture of harassment in workshops was something he would take up with the UP Institute of Creative Writing.

“There was a specific context to my remark that sexual misconduct and plagiarism were “low-hanging fruit.” It was not to dismiss them but to suggest that they were, among human evils, among the most visible and most common (which makes them no less painful to those concerned). I was talking about the possible crimes writers and artists have been accused of, which include murder and treason, and other offenses that injure not just one but many,” Dalisay said.

“I apologize to those victims of sexual harassment who may have seen my remarks as dismissive; they were not meant to be. It is a serious problem we are confronting not only in literature but in society at large.”

2011 plagiarism case

But sexual harassment isn’t the only serious issue that Yuson has found himself involved in. Writer Jaemark Tordecilla had accused him of plagiarism in 2011.

Tordecilla noticed that Yuson lifted several paragraphs from sportswriter Rey Joble’s piece about former PBA commissioner Rudy Salud. Joble’s story was published under GMA News Online, while Yuson had passed off his own version of it to Rogue Magazine.

Yuson was serving as GMA News Online’s editor-at-large then, and was in charge of copyediting Joble’s draft. He explained that since he had rewritten portions of Joble’s work, he thought he was considered to at least be part-author.

While he apologized for his actions, Yuson had merely attributed them to his old age, being overworked, and the pressure of having to meet deadlines. He still continued to write more after, and had even published several more works, like Islands of Words & Other Poems (2015), The Music Child & The Mahjong Queen (2016), and In the Footsteps of St. Ignatius of Loyola (2017), among others.

Withdrawing the republication of Yuson’s book

On September 7, Exploding Galaxies eventually announced that it would no longer push through with promoting or publishing Great Philippine Jungle Energy Café.

“We hear you all. We are sorry for the hurt this has caused our community. We are no longer promoting or releasing this book. As a publisher, we will do better. Thank you for speaking up,” the publisher said.

Exploding Galaxies also promised to “do better” in its mission to put works of Philippine literature back into circulation. But this still begs the question: How can publishers and literary circles do their part in discerning whether or not it is appropriate to promote a piece of work when the individual behind it has caused hurt to many others in the past?

Yuson has yet to comment on the matter himself. – Rappler.com

World.title: Supreme Court acquits Imelda Marcos in 7 counts of graft
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines – The Supreme Court (SC) 1st Division acquitted Imelda Marcos, the mother of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., in her graft cases related to Swiss foundations.

In a decision made public on Wednesday, September 9, the SC division overturned the Sandiganbayan’s November 2018 decision that convicted the 97-year-old former first lady of seven counts of graft.

Play Video

“Accordingly, the Appeal is granted. The November 9, 2018 Decision of the Sandiganbayan in Criminal Case Nos. 17287, 17288, 17289, 17290, 22867, 22868, and 22869 is reversed and set aside. Accused-appellant Imelda R. Marcos is acquitted for the prosecution’s failure to prove her guilt beyond reasonable doubt for violation of Section 3(h) of Republic Act No. 3019, in relation to Article IX, Section 8 of the 1973 Constitution,” said the 50-page ruling penned by Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda.

Associate justices Ramon Paul Hernando, Henri Jean Paul Inting, Ricardo Rosario, and Jose Midas Marquez all concurred in the ruling.

The Marcos matriarch is acquitted four years into the presidential term of her son, who won the presidency in 2022.

The ruling

In its decision, the SC division said the prosecution failed to prove Marcos’ guilt beyond reasonable doubt. Beyond reasonable doubt is the threshold needed to convict an accused in criminal cases.

Marcos was charged with alleged violation of Section 3(h), which has the following elements:

the accused is a public officer

they have direct or indirect financial or pecuniary interest in any business, contract, or transaction

they either intervened or took part in their official capacity or connection with such interest, or they are prohibited from having such interest by the Constitution or by any law

The SC said it’s undisputed that the first element is present, but the second and third elements are contested. The Office of the Ombudsman presented documentary and testimonial evidence that sought to prove Marcos’ financial interest, but the SC said they were “inadmissible and lack probative weight.”

In Marcos’ case, the Sandiganbayan found that she had a financial and pecuniary interest in the foundations based on the Swiss documents. The documents were retrieved from Swiss banks and had been authenticated in accordance with Swiss legal procedure.

However, the SC said the Sandiganbayan erred when it considered the Swiss documents duly authenticated.

“The Court has emphasized that the rule on authentication, more particularly as to private documents, is in place to prevent the inclusion of spurious documents in the body of evidence. Thus, it is settled that private documents are generally inadmissible in evidence unless they are properly authenticated,” said the ruling, adding that the prosecution was not able to present a credible witness who could have testified to the documents’ authenticity.

In addition, even if the SC would ignore the probative weight of the prosecution’s evidence, Marcos must still be acquitted, said the Court. The prosecution, according to the SC, failed to prove that the alleged pecuniary interest was “covered by Section 3(h) of Republic Act No. 3019 and Article IX, Section 7 (then Section 8) of the 1973 Constitution.”

“All told, the prosecution failed to establish that the subject foundations are businesses as the term is ordinarily understood. Any financial or pecuniary interest in the subject foundations is not covered by Section 3(h) of Republic Act No. 3019 and Article IX, Section 7 (then Section 8) of the 1973 Constitution. Doubts on the coverage of the term ‘business’ should be resolved against the State and in favor of the accused-appellant,” said the ruling.

2018 Sandiganbayan decision

In the 2018 decision, the Sandiganbayan sentenced Marcos to six years and one month, up to 11 years, for each count. It also meted the penalty of perpetual disqualification to hold public office.

According to the anti-graft court, Marcos participated in the management of foundations which was a violation of the country’s anti-graft law. The Office of the Ombudsman also found that the public money involved in the private organizations reached $200 million.



It involved seven Swiss foundations. When one foundation closes, the money will be transferred to another, then the foundation will be closed again.

“Pertinently, the [Sandiganbayan] noted that the documents and testimonies presented by the prosecution showed that she has a direct or indirect financial interest in the foundations and has participated in the management of the same,” said the 2018 ruling of the anti-graft court. – Rappler.com

World.title: Search on for missing passengers of vessel off Palawan
World.content:
INQUIRER FILES

PUERTO PRINCESA CITY —Joint personnel of the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) and Coron Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) are conducting search, rescue and emergency operations for missing passengers of an ill-fated passenger ferry that caught fire at sea off Coron town on Wednesday evening (September 9).

The ferry, MV June Aster, owned and operated by Atienza Interisland Ferries, Inc. was carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew when fire erupted while it was 1.2 nautical miles northeast of Barangay Marcilla. The incident was reported to the coast guard at approximately 6:45 p.m.

READ: Passenger ferry caught fire off Coron, Palawan

Article continues after this 

Only 42 passengers have been rescued while five were confirmed dead, according to the latest update from Coast Guard District Palawan.

The survivors were initially brought to a covered court in Barangay Turda and later transferred to ghe Coron District Hospital and other medical facilities while the fatalities’ remains were turned over to the Coron MDRRMO.

The PCG immediately dispatched response teams from coast guard substations in Barangays Turda and Tara in coordination with the Coron MDRRMO and the shipping line which also sent vessels that were docked at Coron port.

CGD Palawan likewise deployed BRP Suluan (MRRV 4406) from El Nido town to augment emergency response.

Coron Mayor Mario Reyes has setup several hotline numbers for relatives of passengers to contact – 09532697909, 09508510441 for Coron District Hospital, and 09953943432 for Coron MDRRMO.

Article continues after this 

Reyes also reported that a 7-year old boy from the ferry was transferred to Culion General Hospital Wednesday night.

The mayor likewise called on the public to give way to the ongoing search and rescue operations, saying responders were primarily focused on securing passengers and others who were affected while details of the incident are still being verified by concerned agencies. /jpv

World.title: Romualdez unfit to travel – PNP
World.content:
Former House Speaker and Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez at the Cardinal Santos Hospital. INQUIRER.net / JASON SIGALES

MANILA, Philippines — Former House Speaker and Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez is not yet medically fit to travel ahead of his scheduled hearing before the Sandiganbayan, according to the Philippine National Police (PNP).

“[The] latest medical certification of Cardinal Santos [last night] is he is not medically fit [to travel],” PNP public information chief Col. Allen Rae Co told the Inquirer in a text message on Thursday morning.

Romualdez was ordered to appear before the anti-graft court for a hearing on his motion to remain in hospital confinement after his arrest last Monday for plunder, a non-bailable charge.

Article continues after this 

READ: Romualdez ordered to appear in Sandiganbayan on Sept. 10

“Syempre, they (Cardinal Santos doctors) also have to coordinate with the CIDG [Criminal Investigation and Detection Group], who will be bringing him supposedly to the Sandiganbayan if he will appear,” Co explained in an interview with GMA’s “Unang Balita” earlier on Thursday.

(Of course, they also have to coordinate with the CIDG, who will be bringing him supposedly to the Sandiganbayan if he will appear.)

“All others sa health status niya, sila lang ang may karapatan magsalita. Ang only confirmation sa amin, cine-certify nila that he is medically unfit to travel,” he added.

(All others regarding his health status, only the doctors have the right to say. The confirmation we have is that they’ve certified that he is medically unfit to travel.)

Article continues after this 

The ex-Congress leader was arrested and booked by the police while on a hospital bed after a purported “cardiovascular event,” unstable blood pressure and an anxiety attack.

Romualdez is accused of “repeatedly receiving… commissions, shares, percentages, kickbacks, commitments and/or other pecuniary benefits” worth P7.44 billion through various government projects from 2022 to 2025.

Article continues after this 

He has since repeatedly denied the allegations against him. /jpv

World.title: Green sea turtle caught in fishing net rescued in Romblon
World.content:
Green sea turtle rescued after getting entangled in fishing net in Romblon. (Photo courtesy of the Municipality of Looc Public Information Office)

CALAPAN CITY — A green sea turtle was rescued after it was found entangled in a fishing net off Barangay Buenavista in the Romblon town of Looc on Wednesday morning (September 9).

The turtle (Chelonia mydas) was spotted by local fisherman Ivan Palacio Conanan Jr., who immediately reported the incident to authorities, according to the Looc Municipal Public Information Office.

READ: Sea turtle hatchling released in Batanes

Article continues after this 

After checking the turtle and confirming that it was in good condition, the responders from the Municipal Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Management Council (MFARMC) and the Coastal Resources Management (CRM) carefully freed it from the fishing net and released it back into the sea.

Photo courtesy of the Municipality of Looc Public Information Office

The rescue team was led by Susan Noche, with MFARMC Vice President Joseph Gregorio and member Richard Fabellar.

According to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), the green sea turtle is classified as an endangered species under DENR Administrative Order No. 2019-09.

Sea turtles and other wildlife are also protected under Republic Act No. 9147, or the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act, which seeks to conserve wildlife species and their habitats. /jpv

World.title: House probe sought into Altai Mining operations in Sibuyan Island
World.content:
Gabriela party-list Rep. Sarah Elago (left), ACT Teachers party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio and Kabataan party-list Rep. Renee Co are shown here in a file photo taken in November 2025 after filing a resolution in the House of Representatives. INQUIRER.net / KRIXIA SUBINGSUBING

CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro — Lawmakers from the Makabayan Bloc on Wednesday (September 9) filed House Resolution No. 1437 seeking a congressional inquiry into the mining operations of Altai Philippines Mining Company (APMC) on Sibuyan Island in Romblon.

The resolution was introduced by Kabataan Party-list Rep. Renee Louise Co, Gabriela Women’s Party Rep. Sarah Jane Elago, and ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio during the second regular session of the 20th Congress.

READ: Mining-free Sibuyan gains ground as local opposition mounts

Article continues after this 

Under HR 1437, the Makabayan lawmakers directs the House Committee on Natural Resources to conduct an investigation, in aid of legislation, of APMC’s activities on the island.

The resolution highlights concerns over potential illegal mining operations, lack of proper community consultations, and environmental destruction in the region.

The resolution explicitly urges the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), through the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB), to immediately suspend all approvals and activities linked to the nickel mining project until free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) is secured from affected communities.

The measure also calls on the Philippine National Police (PNP) to pull out police forces deployed in the area and respect the residents’ constitutional right to peaceful assembly and protest.

Local residents and environmental groups have long opposed APMC’s operations on Sibuyan Island—often dubbed the “Galapagos of Asia” for its rich biodiversity—citing threats to forests, rivers, watersheds, and agricultural livelihoods. /jpv

World.title: Reward offered to find last missing passenger in Tarlac bridge collapse
World.content:
A portion of the Agana Bridge in Barangay Tibag, Tarlac City, lies submerged in rushing waters on Monday, August 31, 2026. Heavy river currents triggered by relentless southwest monsoon or habagat rains undercut the infrastructure, causing the section to collapse on Saturday, August 29. INQUIRER PHOTO / GRIG C. MONTEGRANDE

TARLAC CITY – Tarlac City Mayor Susan Yap has offered a P100,000 reward for information that could help authorities locate the last missing passenger of the SUV that plunged into the river as a section of the Agana Bridge collapsed on August 29.

Search and rescue teams have yet to find Paul Harvey Collado, the SUV’s owner and a supervisor nurse at Jecsons Medical Center. Despite the passage of more than a week, rescuers have not given up the search.

READ: Bodies of 2 SUV passengers found after Tarlac bridge collapse

Article continues after this 

Yap addressed the public in a social media post on Wednesday night, September 9, appealing for information that could help locate Collado.

“Sa panahong puno ng pangamba, ang ating tulong at impormasyon ay maaaring maging daan upang muling makauwi si Paul Harvey sa kanyang pamilya,” Yap said on her official Facebook page.

(In moments of dread, all the help and information you provide may be the solution that would bring Paul Harvey home to his family.)

The bodies of Shanen Tuhao and Shiela Mae Taborlupa have been retrieved from the Bayambang town in Pangasinan where they were located separately on September 1 and on September 5. The remains of James Patrick Taborlupa was found earlier on August 31, off the coast of Lingayen town also in Pangasinan.

The youngest passenger, 20-year old Nataniel Dion, was the only survivor.

Article continues after this 

James Patrick and Shiela Mae Taborlupa, who were siblings, were buried on Tuesday (September 8) at the Loyola Eternal Memorial Park in Tarlac City.

In her post, the mayor also encouraged nearby municipalities and provinces to coordinate with the city government of Tarlac should they receive any information that will help locate Collado. /jpv

World.title: ACT: Higher Pisa scores due to sacrifices made by teachers, students, parents
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — Despite the country’s improved scores in the latest international learning assessment, the Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) said these fail to account for the socioeconomic conditions of learners and educators and ignore how poverty directly undermines learning outcomes.

“The socioeconomic conditions of teachers and students while teaching and learning cannot be separated. It’s difficult to learn while your stomach growls and you’re thinking how you can afford the next meal,” ACT chair Ruby Bernardo said in a statement on Wednesday.

Bernardo added that the improvement in scores should not be credited to the Marcos administration but to the sacrifices of overworked and underpaid teachers, students and parents who “carry the burden of the education system despite systemic neglect.”

Article continues after this 

READ: PH improves rank in international education assessment

In the latest Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) scores released on Tuesday, the Philippines improved its ranking in science, mathematics and reading, outranking 14, 16 and 18 countries, respectively.

ACT, however, warned the public against being obsessed with international rankings, pointing out that the framework of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation (OECD) and Development did not capture local realities due to its “westernized” and “colonial” perspective on education.

“Our conditions are not the same as other countries. There is a difference to our educational system, and the rankings will not mirror our improvement. We must measure our improvement based on the actual situation and needs of our country,” Bernardo said.

READ: Dy credits teachers for PH rise in global student performance

Article continues after this 

ACT urged the government to overhaul the current “colonial, commercialized and repressive” education system and reject foreign-dictated curriculum frameworks.

It also told the government to prioritize a nationalist, scientific and mass-oriented education system grounded in national culture and social needs.

Article continues after this 

Low budget

ACT further criticized the Department of Education (DepEd) for having the lowest national education budget worldwide, which the group claims has neglected the need for schools to have good facilities and equipment. It also said the budget was embarrassing and nothing to be proud of.

The Department of Budget and Management has touted the P1.326 trillion allocated for basic and higher education in the proposed 2027 national budget as a reflection that the education sector ranks among the government’s top spending priorities.

ACT, however, said the education budget only falls under 3 percent to 4 percent of the country’s gross domestic product, “far from the amount needed to fulfill the needs of the country such as the amount of teachers, classrooms, education support personnel, and equipment.”

“That’s why alongside additions to the education budget, we should improve the state of living in the country, raise the salary of teachers and other personnel, and provide proper support to learners,” Bernardo said.

DepEd’s next step

The DepEd, in wake of the improved scores, said it would roll out Pisa for Schools, an OECD assessment service that provides school-level performance benchmarked against international standards.

“This can help us understand more clearly what is happening inside our schools and where support is most needed,” said Education Secretary Sonny Angara in a statement on Wednesday. “The objective is to turn better data into better decisions, so that improvements in our national results are felt by learners in the classroom.”

According to him, the service generates internationally comparable results for individual schools, measuring the same core competencies of 15-year-old students in reading, mathematics, and science.

“Our goal is not to create another ranking. It is to give schools information they can act on. If we know more precisely where learners are struggling, we can better target interventions, strengthen teaching, and direct resources where they can make the greatest difference,” said Angara.
